Glassnode counted nearly $3 billion of ETF inflows from Sept. 21 to Oct. 6, and Farside Investors’ data since then shows a reversal. A net $859 million flowed out over six sessions from Oct. 7 through Oct. 14, including $261.4 million on Oct. 14.

Bitcoin is holding near a cost-basis zone while redemptions hit the vehicles tied to that zone. Either remaining investors and spot bids are absorbing the selling, or the market grows more vulnerable as new demand fades.

Köymen said what breaks the range “is a catalyst.” Back-to-back hot prints, with core PPI up 0.7% on top of a firmer CPI, have made the Oct. 28 Fed meeting two-way.

Futures priced hike odds near 50-50 immediately upon CPI and now lean toward a hold, with estimates of roughly 29% to 34% across Oct. 15 reports. September PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, lands on Oct. 29, a day later.

The Fed raised its target range to 3.75% to 4.00% on Sept. 16, and its September projections put the end-2026 policy rate at 4.1% against 3.8% in June. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks in Bangkok on Oct. 16, his last appearance before the blackout, and Köymen expects his remarks to move markets little.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

Huang called Thursday's PPI “a key near-term risk,” since a stronger print would reinforce worries about additional tightening and could weigh on Bitcoin “through higher Treasury yields, a stronger dollar and weaker risk appetite.”

Related Reading Bitcoin plunges to $81,300 support as Fed hike odds hit 55% amid $100 million crypto wipeout

The 10-year Treasury yield fell to about 5.087%, and the dollar retreated from an 18-month high, as safe-haven bond demand tied to worries over AI-company financing offset inflation.

Köymen noted that yields near their 2002 high and a firm dollar have historically weighed on Bitcoin, but it has held up well and trades above its September-high level. He said that the rate path drives price, and any single day's ETF flow carries less weight.

Gasoline supplied more than half of the monthly CPI increase, and energy accounted for more than 80% of the rise in final-demand producer goods prices, with producer gasoline up 20.3%.

A Fed that treats the energy surge as temporary has room to hold, and the 0.7% core PPI gain weighs against that reading.

Köymen said the Nov. 3 elections add event risk, though historically other forces have driven Bitcoin's longer-term direction.

A CryptoQuant analysis shows Bitcoin gaining 24.5%, 44.9% and 92.3% over the 12 months from the 2014, 2018 and 2022 midterms, and falling about 45.5% in the first month once the 2018 election had passed.

Three cycles under different monetary regimes are too few to isolate an election effect. Huang added that markets will watch whether President Donald Trump continues to signal supportive measures for crypto, and that absent further crypto-specific policy catalysts, “inflation will remain the primary driver.”

A volatility check shows the box is narrower than the full distribution of outcomes. Using 35.46% 30-day implied volatility reported by Derivasys and an $83,000 starting price, a one-standard-deviation move through Nov. 3 spans roughly $76,300 to $89,700.

Bitcoin could temporarily trade below $80,000 and finish the period inside the box, making $80,000 to $88,000 the zone where supply and demand concentrate, separate from any corridor options guarantee .

If the Fed holds on Oct. 28, guidance avoids a hawkish surprise and ETF outflows stabilize, the range survives into the midterms. A move through $88,000 would need new demand to absorb supply from holders returning to break-even, and short liquidations near that level could accelerate a breakout that lasts when spot buying joins it.

If inflation persistence lifts expected rates and Bitcoin closes below $79,960 , Huang's breakdown scenario opens, and $78,000 becomes the next test with the remaining long liquidations just below $80,000 in play.

The drop from $80,000 to $78,000 is 2.5%, and the larger risk is a $78,000 floor that fails to attract buyers.

The Oct. 28 decision, PCE on Oct. 29, and the Nov. 3 vote fall in sequence, and the first two matter more than the third in deciding whether the range survives.

Policy U.S. judge rejects Gemini’s appeal to void $5 million settlement despite CFTC backing

The crypto exchange already paid up, but a court order and restrictions from its 2025 settlement will not be lifted even though the CFTC said the case should have never been presented.

By Olivier Acuna | Edited by Sheldon Reback Oct 16, 2026, 5:36 a.m. EDT

2 min read Make preferred on Share 

A judge denied the Winkelovoss' appeal against a $5 million settlement they already paid. (Jesse Hamilton/CoinDesk) Summary Show A federal judge rejected a joint request from Gemini and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to overturn the crypto exchange’s $5 million settlement. The judge ruled that the CFTC’s changed position did not justify undoing the January 2025 agreement and rejected Gemini’s claim that regulators had coerced it into settling.

A U.S. federal judge rejected an unusual joint request from crypto exchange Gemini and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to overturn a $5 million settlement , even though the regulator said the case should not have been brought.

Federal Judge Alvin Hellerstein ruled Thursday that the CFTC’s decision to reverse its position on the case was not enough to undo Gemini’s January 2025 settlement. He also rejected Gemini’s argument that it had been coerced into settling by regulators.

Gemini, founded by Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, has already paid the $5 million. The ruling also keeps the exchange under a court order prohibiting it from misleading the CFTC or publicly denying the settlement's findings.

The decision is significant because it shows that a friendlier approach to crypto regulation in Washington D.C. is not retroactive. It does not automatically erase earlier court judgments, even though the regulator and the company agree they should be withdrawn.

Gemini can still operate in the U.S. and introduce new products, but the ruling means it must live with the terms of its 2025 settlement as it shifts its business toward the American market.

The CFTC sued Gemini in 2023, alleging it misled regulators during a 2017 review of a proposed bitcoin futures contract. Gemini, which has not responded to a request for comment on Thursday’s ruling, settled three weeks before the trial without admitting or denying the allegations.

“Gemini litigated the case for approximately three years, and then, despite the preceding facts, made the calculated decision to settle the case shortly before trial,” the judge wrote.

Earlier this year, Gemini announced plans to exit the U.K., European Union and Australia and cut 25% of its workforce as it shifted resources toward the U.S. market and prediction markets. The company said it would continue operating in Singapore.

Written by William Suberg staff writer Edited by Yohan Yun staff editor Written by William Suberg staff writer Edited by Yohan Yun staff editor

Bitcoin may seek 20-month trend line reclaim before new record highs: CryptoQuant

Markets Published Oct 16, 2026 Bitcoin’s market cycle signals tool showed BTC price action copying history, possibly preparing to reclaim a key moving average before testing new highs.

Bitcoin is attempting to break through an “inflection frontier” that has historically triggered runs to new macro highs.

Data from onchain analytics platform CryptoQuant reveals that BTC/USD has begun a fresh battle with its 20-month simple moving average (SMA).

The 20-month SMA, at $87,165 as of Oct. 16, is the trend line around which the popular Bollinger Bands metric is constructed. This in turn forms the basis for CryptoQuant’s market cycle signals tool, which seeks to pinpoint Bitcoin’s position within its market cycle.

Bollinger Bands uses standard deviation to add an upper and lower band around the 20-month SMA. Currently, these sit at $121,640 and $52,694, respectively. CryptoQuant’s indicator describes the zone between the lower band and SMA as an “accumulation base,” while the SMA itself is referred to as an “inflection frontier,” a previous point of investor capitulation as price broke below it from above, most recently in December 2025.

BTC/USD one-month chart with Bollinger Bands. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

With Bitcoin now preparing to challenge the capitulation zone from below, history shows that successful breakouts have led to new cycle highs.

“Just over a year after the all-time high (ATH) of $124,709 on October 6, 2025, the market has concluded its ‘reset,’” CryptoQuant contributor GugaOnChain summarized in a blog post.

While Bollinger Bands are not intended to offer buy and sell signals, market cycle signals sees “smart money” taking profit once BTC/USD reaches its upper band. While this currently sits just below Bitcoin’s most recent all-time high of $126,200 from October 2025, CryptoQuant sees the next rally continuing beyond that level.

“While retail fears the current $82,442, thinking it’s the ‘top,’ the on-chain indicator BTC: Market Cycle Signals reveals that we are just warming up,” GugaOnChain added, referring to a current BTC price support zone .

Bitcoin market cycle signals chart. Source: CryptoQuant

The 20-month SMA has confluence with Bitcoin’s 2026 opening level at $87,490, boosting its strength as resistance. As Cointelegraph reported , large walls of ask liquidity remain in the vicinity across exchange order books.

CryptoQuant maintains a broadly optimistic stance on Bitcoin’s emerging bull market despite crypto and risk assets navigating macroeconomic headwinds .

Related: Here’s what happened in crypto today

This week, contributor XWIN Research Japan flagged data from three onchain metrics that they said gave reason for “cautious optimism” for bullish momentum to return through the end of October.

In late August, CEO Ki Young Ju officially stated that the bear market was “over” based on readings from the bull-bear market cycle indicator. This uses composite data from several onchain profitability metrics, and shows bullish momentum accelerating with a reading of 0.186 on its scale versus 0.042 in August.

Bitcoin bull-bear market cycle Indicator. Source: CryptoQuant

What Is a Hardware Wallet? Crypto Cold Storage Explained

Hardware wallets keep your crypto keys offline. Learn how devices from Ledger, Trezor and others protect your Bitcoin and Ethereum.

By Decrypt Agent Edited by Stephen Graves

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Hardware wallets are physical devices that keep crypto private keys offline, signing transactions internally so the keys never touch an internet-connected device.

They are not hack-proof: a Coldcard firmware bug and tampered Ledger devices sold through a reseller both led to major losses in 2026.

Wallet manufacturers are looking to future-proof their devices for a future of agentic finance and quantum computing.

There's an old saying in crypto: "not your keys, not your coins." When you leave Bitcoin , Ethereum or any other cryptocurrency on an exchange , the exchange holds the private keys that control those funds. If it gets hacked, goes bust or freezes withdrawals, you may have no way to get them back.

The obvious fix is to hold your own keys, which is called self-custody . That brings its own problem, though. A private key stored in a software wallet on an internet-connected phone or laptop can be stolen by malware, phishing sites and remote attackers.

Hardware wallets were built to solve this. They're small physical devices that keep your private keys offline, so you can sign crypto transactions without your keys ever touching a device connected to the internet. In this guide we'll explain what hardware wallets are, how they work, who makes them, and where the technology is heading after an eventful 2026.

A hardware wallet is a dedicated physical device, usually about the size of a USB stick or credit card, that generates and stores the private keys for your crypto. It's a form of "cold storage," because the keys stay offline. A "hot wallet" like a browser extension or mobile app is the opposite.

One common misconception is that your coins live on the device. They don't. Your crypto always lives on the blockchain. The hardware wallet holds the keys that prove you own it and let you move it.

The category dates back more than a decade. Trezor, made by Czech firm SatoshiLabs, calls itself the inventor of the hardware wallet in 2013. France-based Ledger was founded in 2014 and has since reported sales of more than eight million devices .

When you set up a hardware wallet, it gives you a "seed phrase" of 12 to 24 words. Anyone who has those words can recreate your wallet and take your funds, so never photograph them, type them into a website, or save them to cloud storage.

When you first switch on a hardware wallet, it uses a random number generator to create your private keys. A seed phrase backs them up, and a PIN code protects the device.

When you want to send crypto, you build the transaction in companion software on your computer or phone, such as Ledger Wallet (formerly Ledger Live), Trezor Suite or Sparrow. The software sends the unsigned transaction to the hardware wallet. You check the details on the device's own screen and confirm with a physical button or touchscreen. The device then signs the transaction inside its own hardware and sends back only the signature. The private key never leaves the device.

Devices connect in different ways, and each comes with security trade-offs:

Many devices also use a secure element, a tamper-resistant chip like the ones in passports and bank cards, to guard keys against physical attacks.

"Clear signing" means a wallet shows transaction details in plain language rather than raw code, so you know what you're approving. That matters because scammers often trick people into signing malicious smart contract approvals.

Their main advantage is isolation. Even if your laptop is full of malware, an attacker can't take your keys out of a well-designed hardware wallet or approve a transaction without you physically confirming it.

Hardware wallets have improved over the years, evolving from miniscule screens and clunky interfaces to modern devices that incorporate Bluetooth, NFC and even touchscreens and cameras.

Hardware wallets are also starting to do more than just crypto storage. Ledger added stablecoin yield through Kiln in April 2025, Tangem followed with Aave later that year, and Trezor launched native stablecoin yield through Morpho vaults in May 2026.

Like any device, hardware wallets can be compromised—something that became painfully apparent in July 2026, when attackers took advantage of a five-year-old Coldcard firmware bug that had weakened the randomness used to create seeds.

According to TRM Labs , the exploit drained about 1,816 BTC, worth around $116 million, from more than 5,200 addresses. Updating the firmware doesn't fix seeds that were already created, so affected users have to move their funds to a new wallet.

Hardware wallets are also vulnerable to physical hacks. In October 2026, Ledger revealed that an unauthorized chip implanted in devices sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis was able to read seed phrases as they were entered during setup and transmit them to an attacker. The investigation followed reports that some $86 million had been drained from Ledger wallet users.

Although the firm’s own Secure Element hardware had not been compromised, its reseller network created a centralized point of vulnerability that attackers were able to exploit by tampering with the device to add their own hidden chip.

Ledger subsequently halted distribution via resellers in seven Asian markets , while a European reseller, MediaMarkt, also stopped sales following reports of unauthorized implants. Rival manufacturer Trezor also wound up its reseller program as a “precautionary measure.”

Another point of vulnerability is third-party vendors and shipping partners, with several hacks and exploits exposing customer data including addresses. While no funds were lost in those cases, leaked customer details feed phishing scams and even physical " wrench attacks ," where criminals threaten crypto holders in person.

For most people, phishing and a poorly stored seed phrase are much bigger risks than someone hacking the device itself.

Always buy hardware wallets straight from the manufacturer's official website, and avoid second-hand devices and unofficial marketplace listings. As the CryptoBilis incident demonstrates, even authorized resellers represent a point of vulnerability that attackers can exploit, and it’s likely that manufacturers will rethink their reseller programs in its aftermath.

Hardware wallets are also starting to do more than just crypto storage. Ledger added stablecoin yield through Kiln in April 2025, Tangem followed with Aave later that year, and Trezor launched native stablecoin yield through Morpho vaults in May 2026.

Like any device, hardware wallets can be compromised—something that became painfully apparent in July 2026, when attackers took advantage of a five-year-old Coldcard firmware bug that had weakened the randomness used to create seeds.

According to TRM Labs , the exploit drained about 1,816 BTC, worth around $116 million, from more than 5,200 addresses. Updating the firmware doesn't fix seeds that were already created, so affected users have to move their funds to a new wallet.

Hardware wallets are also vulnerable to physical hacks. In October 2026, Ledger revealed that an unauthorized chip implanted in devices sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis was able to read seed phrases as they were entered during setup and transmit them to an attacker. The investigation followed reports that some $86 million had been drained from Ledger wallet users.

Although the firm’s own Secure Element hardware had not been compromised, its reseller network created a centralized point of vulnerability that attackers were able to exploit by tampering with the device to add their own hidden chip.

Ledger subsequently halted distribution via resellers in seven Asian markets , while a European reseller, MediaMarkt, also stopped sales following reports of unauthorized implants. Rival manufacturer Trezor also wound up its reseller program as a “precautionary measure.”

Another point of vulnerability is third-party vendors and shipping partners, with several hacks and exploits exposing customer data including addresses. While no funds were lost in those cases, leaked customer details feed phishing scams and even physical " wrench attacks ," where criminals threaten crypto holders in person.

For most people, phishing and a poorly stored seed phrase are much bigger risks than someone hacking the device itself.

Always buy hardware wallets straight from the manufacturer's official website, and avoid second-hand devices and unofficial marketplace listings. As the CryptoBilis incident demonstrates, even authorized resellers represent a point of vulnerability that attackers can exploit, and it’s likely that manufacturers will rethink their reseller programs in its aftermath.

Markets MSCI approves rules that could eject Strategy, Metaplanet from equity indexes

The rules proposed in August would see companies that exist mainly to hold investments as no longer eligible for index inclusion.

By Omkar Godbole | Edited by Sheldon Reback Oct 16, 2026, 4:34 a.m. EDT

3 min read Make preferred on Share 

MSCI's new rules raises index exclusion risk for Strategy and Metaplanet. (Shutterstock) Summary Show MSCI finalized rules that could remove Strategy, Metaplanet and other investment-heavy companies from its global equity indexes after trading closes on Nov. 30. The affected firms will be named on Nov. 11. JPMorgan analysts have estimated that Strategy’s exclusion could prompt about $2.8 billion in stock outflows, though index funds’ forced sales would affect the company’s shares, not its bitcoin holdings.

MSCI, one of the world's biggest stock index providers, finalized rules proposed in August that could remove shares of leading bitcoin BTC $82,501.32 -holding companies Strategy MSTR and Metaplanet (3350) from its global equity indexes.

Under the rules announced Thursday , companies that mostly hold investments rather than running a real business will be deemed ineligible for MSCI's Global Investable Market Indexes. The final list of affected firms is due Nov. 11 and the change takes effect at the close of Nov. 30.

The decision is important because it affects demand for the companies’ shares. Many investors gain exposure to stock markets by placing their money in funds that track an index. When a company is added to the index, those funds must buy its stock. When it is removed, they must sell, whatever the fund managers think of the company.

"The MSCI episode highlights a growing tension between traditional index construction and the rise of companies that treat Bitcoin as a core treasury asset rather than a secondary holding,” decentralized infrastructure network ZEROBASE said on X . “Passive capital has become an important source of demand for these stocks; any sustained reduction in that bid could tighten the equity-issuance window that several of them rely on to fund further purchases."

The risk is biggest for Tysons Corner, Virginia-based Strategy, the largest publicly listed bitcoin holder, with 848,250 BTC worth about $69.67 billion, according to Bitcoin Treasuries. It tends to fund its purchases by selling preferred shares such as STRC and STRK .

JPMorgan analysts have estimated that index exclusion could trigger outflows of about $2.8 billion from MSTR stock. The shares closed at $151.29 on Thursday, down about 72% from their record high of $543 in November 2024. Tokyo-based Metplanet, which closed at 277 yen ($1.75) on Friday, peaked at 1,930 yen in June 2025, according to TradingView.

Any selling would hit the shares, not bitcoin. The funds would be dumping the stock, which does not necessarily mean Strategy would sell its bitcoin.

But weaker demand for the shares could make it harder for these companies to raise the money they use to buy more bitcoin, a strategy they have long pursued to stack up more coins.

Strategy's founder, Michael Saylor, has described the company as an operating business with a software arm, and its bitcoin treasury as a distinct business segment. He has rejected comparisons with investment funds. Strategy, originally MicroStrategy, sells business intelligence software to companies including Coca-Cola and Porsche.

MSCI already excludes investment funds and similar vehicles. The new rules extend that to companies that look like them.

First, MSCI checks whether a company has substantial operating assets, meaning assets tied to a real business. If it fails, the company faces a second test based on five financial ratios covering expenses, cash flow, changes in asset values and reliance on outside financing. A company flagged on four or more of the five is ineligible.

To avoid constant churn in the index, MSCI has added buffers. A member is removed only if it fails the screen in each of its two most recent annual filing periods. A company outside the index is blocked from joining if it fails in either of its two most recent periods.

In a first test run using May 2026 data, MSCI flagged three companies for possible removal from its ACWI Investable Market Index. They were Strategy, Metaplanet and Yellow Cake, a U.K. uranium investment company.

MSCI is also ending the temporary measures it announced in October 2025 for companies with digital assets making up 50% or more of total assets. Those measures froze increases in the share counts used in the index and put off additions and size-segment moves for those companies. From the November review, they will be judged under the new rules instead.

posts.content:
News Bitcoin News Image by CryptoSlate Lending Bearish

Native Bitcoin collateral on Aave triggers WBTC pool deficit

Hub suppliers would finance fast exits before permissioned buyers acquire the vaults, with escrow shortfalls reported as deficits.

By Liam 'Akiba' Wright Editor-in-Chief • CryptoSlate

01 Babylon’s Aave V4 proposal would keep collateral native on Bitcoin while borrowing WBTC to settle open liquidations. 02 Hub suppliers would finance escrow until a permissioned buyer takes over; direct keepers could fund their own liquidation. 03 Escrow shortfalls would become Hub deficits, while the proposal leaves a funded WBTC backstop unspecified. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Aave’s proposed native Bitcoin lending market would keep collateral in Bitcoin while borrowing wrapped Bitcoin (WBTC) to pay outside liquidators immediately. Suppliers financing those payouts would face any settlement shortfall without funded protection.

The design in Babylon Labs’ Oct. 14 proposal separates fast liquidation from the slower redemption of Bitcoin collateral. Its open route draws WBTC from Aave’s shared liquidity pool, called a Hub, until a permissioned buyer takes over the vault.

A direct keeper route lets an authorized operator finance repayment and redeem the BTC itself.

The Aave Request for Comment lists feedback, a conditional Snapshot vote, and an eventual on-chain proposal with full risk parameters as subsequent steps.

A borrower would lock BTC in an individual Taproot vault on Bitcoin, and Aave would recognize it through a restricted ERC-20 accounting token that cannot be traded between users. The WBTC used for liquidation settlement is a separate asset.

When a position becomes liquidatable, an outside liquidator would repay the borrower’s debt asset through the integration’s adapter. The seized vault would then be sold to the BTC Vault Swap Spoke, a settlement component that draws WBTC from an Aave Hub and pays the liquidator at an oracle-based price minus a sell discount.

That exchange lets the liquidator leave with a transferable asset in the same transaction. The Swap Spoke would keep the vault in escrow and owe interest on the borrowed WBTC.

An arbitrageur with redemption rights would later acquire the vault by repaying the draw and accrued interest, then claim the BTC on Bitcoin.

Hub liquidity funds the escrow before an arbitrageur buys it. After that purchase, the arbitrageur has committed capital and must wait for Bitcoin redemption, which takes multiple days through the challenge window.

Authorized application vault keepers can repay the borrower’s debt and redeem the seized vault directly to their own Bitcoin key, bypassing the Swap Spoke’s Hub draw. On that route, the keeper finances repayment and the wait for BTC settlement.

Liquidation route Immediate settlement Who finances the wait? Open route through the Swap Spoke Liquidator receives Hub-funded WBTC; vault enters escrow Hub liquidity until purchase, then the permissioned arbitrageur until Bitcoin settlement Direct application keeper Keeper repays debt and initiates redemption to its Bitcoin key The keeper, without the Swap Spoke’s WBTC funding draw If the borrower’s entire debt is cleared before that vault’s value is consumed, the liquidator must compensate the borrower for the remainder in WBTC at the liquidation-bonus discount. Even the direct keeper route can require WBTC for this surplus payment.

The Swap Spoke’s WBTC borrowing creates a second debt alongside the borrower’s original loan. Its repayment depends on the escrowed vault attracting an eligible buyer on the specified terms.

If the vault’s current value no longer covers its Hub debt, an arbitrageur can still buy it. The repayment is capped at the vault’s value less a reserved arbitrageur margin, with the unpaid balance reported to the Hub as a deficit in the same transaction.

The reserved margin preserves an incentive to buy the vault and allows the mechanism to complete a purchase while recognizing a loss.

Aave V4’s deficit documentation separates recognition from elimination. Covering a deficit consumes supplied Hub shares belonging to an authorized active Spoke, so someone’s supplied capital must bear the cost of restoring the accounting balance.

TokenLogic’s September coverage framework places deficit exposure with suppliers of the specific Hub asset drawn and tracks the originating Spoke separately.

Under that framework, a shortfall on the proposed WBTC draw would affect suppliers of that Hub asset unless allocated protection absorbed it.

The framework describes DAO deficit offsets as the first loss layer before Umbrella protection where that protection is configured. Its initial recommendations cover three Core lending markets : WETH, USDC and USDT.

WBTC financing falls outside that initial scope, and the Babylon proposal does not specify a funded WBTC backstop.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

That leaves the final funding Hub, draw limits, and any dedicated protection material to the market’s eventual risk allocation. The proposed loss-recording mechanism leaves backstop funding as a separate decision.

Aave and Babylon’s proposed WBTC settlement leaves any escrow shortfall with Hub suppliers unless funded protection absorbs the loss. Liquidity can constrain the open route before a deficit occurs. Babylon’s public safety documentation says permissionless liquidations revert if Hub WBTC liquidity or the Swap Spoke’s allowance is insufficient.

Registered arbitrageurs can still use direct redemption, but the available liquidators narrow.

The dependency illustrates the trade-off: Hub funding broadens liquidation participation, while the direct route relies on operators already equipped to claim Bitcoin and finance settlement.

Permission to trigger a liquidation also differs from permission to redeem the BTC. Redemption rights are committed into a vault’s spending structure.

Related Reading You can borrow against Bitcoin without selling it, but there’s a catch

Babylon’s own SCRIPT framework assesses freedom from third-party censorship separately from title retention and collateral backing. The proposed combination of an open liquidation trigger, permissioned redeemers, and pause powers makes that distinction consequential for exit availability.

Babylon’s safety documentation gives depositors or delegated operators a way to dispute an invalid claim using saved vault-specific artifacts, which requires timely action. A transitional Security Council can block a payout but cannot redirect the Bitcoin.

The ARFC assigns governance of both Spokes and their funding Hubs to Aave DAO. It also assigns a separate Swap Spoke configuration role to a 2-of-3 multisig of LlamaRisk, Babylon Labs and Aave Labs. Babylon protocol governance would control its configuration and actor sets through a public timelock.

The ARFC says a TBV freeze preserves exits while a pause stops them. Public-testnet documentation instead describes soft and full pauses, with already-available Bitcoin recovery paths retaining separate protections.

The BabylonSpoke pull request proposes manager-gated liquidation capped by collateral amount. The final configuration and follow-up security reviews remain material to deployment.

Babylon says audit engagements covered five components and that Coinspect, ABDK, and Zellic are re-auditing finalized changes before mainnet, with follow-up reports to be shared when finalized.

For borrowers, the outstanding settings determine how much debt their vaults can support and what liquidation costs. For Hub suppliers, the crucial terms are how much WBTC the settlement component can draw, how repayment is priced, and what capital would absorb a shortfall.

Those terms will determine the financial risk that sits alongside the proposed native Bitcoin collateral.

Native Bitcoin collateral on Aave triggers WBTC pool deficit

Hub suppliers would finance fast exits before permissioned buyers acquire the vaults, with escrow shortfalls reported as deficits.

By Liam 'Akiba' Wright Editor-in-Chief • CryptoSlate

01 Babylon’s Aave V4 proposal would keep collateral native on Bitcoin while borrowing WBTC to settle open liquidations. 02 Hub suppliers would finance escrow until a permissioned buyer takes over; direct keepers could fund their own liquidation. 03 Escrow shortfalls would become Hub deficits, while the proposal leaves a funded WBTC backstop unspecified. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Aave’s proposed native Bitcoin lending market would keep collateral in Bitcoin while borrowing wrapped Bitcoin (WBTC) to pay outside liquidators immediately. Suppliers financing those payouts would face any settlement shortfall without funded protection.

The design in Babylon Labs’ Oct. 14 proposal separates fast liquidation from the slower redemption of Bitcoin collateral. Its open route draws WBTC from Aave’s shared liquidity pool, called a Hub, until a permissioned buyer takes over the vault.

A direct keeper route lets an authorized operator finance repayment and redeem the BTC itself.

The Aave Request for Comment lists feedback, a conditional Snapshot vote, and an eventual on-chain proposal with full risk parameters as subsequent steps.

A borrower would lock BTC in an individual Taproot vault on Bitcoin, and Aave would recognize it through a restricted ERC-20 accounting token that cannot be traded between users. The WBTC used for liquidation settlement is a separate asset.

When a position becomes liquidatable, an outside liquidator would repay the borrower’s debt asset through the integration’s adapter. The seized vault would then be sold to the BTC Vault Swap Spoke, a settlement component that draws WBTC from an Aave Hub and pays the liquidator at an oracle-based price minus a sell discount.

That exchange lets the liquidator leave with a transferable asset in the same transaction. The Swap Spoke would keep the vault in escrow and owe interest on the borrowed WBTC.

An arbitrageur with redemption rights would later acquire the vault by repaying the draw and accrued interest, then claim the BTC on Bitcoin.

Hub liquidity funds the escrow before an arbitrageur buys it. After that purchase, the arbitrageur has committed capital and must wait for Bitcoin redemption, which takes multiple days through the challenge window.

Authorized application vault keepers can repay the borrower’s debt and redeem the seized vault directly to their own Bitcoin key, bypassing the Swap Spoke’s Hub draw. On that route, the keeper finances repayment and the wait for BTC settlement.

Liquidation route Immediate settlement Who finances the wait? Open route through the Swap Spoke Liquidator receives Hub-funded WBTC; vault enters escrow Hub liquidity until purchase, then the permissioned arbitrageur until Bitcoin settlement Direct application keeper Keeper repays debt and initiates redemption to its Bitcoin key The keeper, without the Swap Spoke’s WBTC funding draw If the borrower’s entire debt is cleared before that vault’s value is consumed, the liquidator must compensate the borrower for the remainder in WBTC at the liquidation-bonus discount. Even the direct keeper route can require WBTC for this surplus payment.

The Swap Spoke’s WBTC borrowing creates a second debt alongside the borrower’s original loan. Its repayment depends on the escrowed vault attracting an eligible buyer on the specified terms.

If the vault’s current value no longer covers its Hub debt, an arbitrageur can still buy it. The repayment is capped at the vault’s value less a reserved arbitrageur margin, with the unpaid balance reported to the Hub as a deficit in the same transaction.

The reserved margin preserves an incentive to buy the vault and allows the mechanism to complete a purchase while recognizing a loss.

Aave V4’s deficit documentation separates recognition from elimination. Covering a deficit consumes supplied Hub shares belonging to an authorized active Spoke, so someone’s supplied capital must bear the cost of restoring the accounting balance.

TokenLogic’s September coverage framework places deficit exposure with suppliers of the specific Hub asset drawn and tracks the originating Spoke separately.

Under that framework, a shortfall on the proposed WBTC draw would affect suppliers of that Hub asset unless allocated protection absorbed it.

The framework describes DAO deficit offsets as the first loss layer before Umbrella protection where that protection is configured. Its initial recommendations cover three Core lending markets : WETH, USDC and USDT.

WBTC financing falls outside that initial scope, and the Babylon proposal does not specify a funded WBTC backstop.

That leaves the final funding Hub, draw limits, and any dedicated protection material to the market’s eventual risk allocation. The proposed loss-recording mechanism leaves backstop funding as a separate decision.

Aave and Babylon’s proposed WBTC settlement leaves any escrow shortfall with Hub suppliers unless funded protection absorbs the loss. Liquidity can constrain the open route before a deficit occurs. Babylon’s public safety documentation says permissionless liquidations revert if Hub WBTC liquidity or the Swap Spoke’s allowance is insufficient.

Registered arbitrageurs can still use direct redemption, but the available liquidators narrow.

The dependency illustrates the trade-off: Hub funding broadens liquidation participation, while the direct route relies on operators already equipped to claim Bitcoin and finance settlement.

Permission to trigger a liquidation also differs from permission to redeem the BTC. Redemption rights are committed into a vault’s spending structure.

Related Reading You can borrow against Bitcoin without selling it, but there’s a catch

Babylon’s own SCRIPT framework assesses freedom from third-party censorship separately from title retention and collateral backing. The proposed combination of an open liquidation trigger, permissioned redeemers, and pause powers makes that distinction consequential for exit availability.

Babylon’s safety documentation gives depositors or delegated operators a way to dispute an invalid claim using saved vault-specific artifacts, which requires timely action. A transitional Security Council can block a payout but cannot redirect the Bitcoin.

The ARFC assigns governance of both Spokes and their funding Hubs to Aave DAO. It also assigns a separate Swap Spoke configuration role to a 2-of-3 multisig of LlamaRisk, Babylon Labs and Aave Labs. Babylon protocol governance would control its configuration and actor sets through a public timelock.

The ARFC says a TBV freeze preserves exits while a pause stops them. Public-testnet documentation instead describes soft and full pauses, with already-available Bitcoin recovery paths retaining separate protections.

The BabylonSpoke pull request proposes manager-gated liquidation capped by collateral amount. The final configuration and follow-up security reviews remain material to deployment.

Babylon says audit engagements covered five components and that Coinspect, ABDK, and Zellic are re-auditing finalized changes before mainnet, with follow-up reports to be shared when finalized.

For borrowers, the outstanding settings determine how much debt their vaults can support and what liquidation costs. For Hub suppliers, the crucial terms are how much WBTC the settlement component can draw, how repayment is priced, and what capital would absorb a shortfall.

Those terms will determine the financial risk that sits alongside the proposed native Bitcoin collateral.

Written by Zoltan Vardai staff writer Edited by Yohan Yun staff editor Written by Zoltan Vardai staff writer Edited by Yohan Yun staff editor

Capital B reports $78M H1 loss driven by Bitcoin impairment charge

Latest News Published Oct 16, 2026 Europe’s second-largest Bitcoin treasury raised $30 million and increased its Bitcoin holdings by 11% in the first half of 2026, despite reporting a $75 million Bitcoin impairment loss.

France-listed Bitcoin treasury company Capital B reported a net loss of 69.5 million euro ($78 million) for the first half of 2026, driven by a Bitcoin impairment charge of $75.8 million.

The impairment reflected Bitcoin (BTC) prices as of June 30 and had no direct cash impact, according to the company’s first-half 2026 report , published Thursday.

Still, Capital B’s consolidated revenue rose 3.5% year-over-year to $6.5 million, while adjusted EBITDA was negative $1.2 million. EBITDA measures a company’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization.

The results show that the European Bitcoin treasury firm continued raising funds to fuel its Bitcoin accumulation despite the accounting losses. Capital B announced capital raises totaling $30 million in the first half of the year and increased its Bitcoin holdings by 11%, from 2,823 BTC in January to 3,139 BTC by the end of June.

The company’s total holdings subsequently reached 3,538 Bitcoin by Sept. 30, marking a 25% increase from the beginning of the year. Capital B’s treasury is currently worth $290 million, ranking it as the world’s 25th-largest corporate Bitcoin treasury and Europe’s second-largest by holdings, following Germany-based Bitcoin Group, according to Bitcointreasuries .

Capital B’s stock price rose by 0.5% in early morning trading on Friday, but was down 25% year-to-date, according to Yahoo Finance .

In July, Capital B approved a 10-for-1 reverse stock split aimed at broadening its institutional investor base. In June, its shareholders approved up to $120 billion in financing capacity, including equity and credit instruments, to support the company’s Bitcoin accumulation strategy.

posts.title: Fed Chair Warsh’s Bangkok Speech: 4 Key Takeaways and What They Mean for Bitcoin
posts.titleVi: Fed Chair Warsh’s Bangkok Speech: 4 Key Takeaways and What They Mean for Bitcoin
posts.summary: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh delivered one of the week’s most closely watched central-bank appearances on Friday morning, following the hotter-than-expected CPI and PPI reports from earlier this month that revived fears of another US rate increase.
posts.summaryVi: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh delivered one of the week’s most closely watched central-bank appearances on Friday morning, following the hotter-than-expected CPI and PPI reports from earlier this month that revived fears of another US rate increase.
posts.content:
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh delivered one of the week’s most closely watched central-bank appearances on Friday morning, following the hotter-than-expected CPI and PPI reports from earlier this month that revived fears of another US rate increase.

Speaking alongside IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva at the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Warsh refused to signal clearly on the Fed’s next move.

Fed’s Chair reiterated that the central bank intends to “deliver price stability” and reminded that it removed “a close of accommodation” with September’s 25-basis-point hike. However, he explained that he does not “prejudge meetings” and would not announce in advance what he might do at the remaining 2026 gatherings.

This was particularly important for markets after the recent CPI and PPI readings, which showed that the inflation scare has not gone away. Recall that September CPI accelerated to 3.7%, higher than expected, and the odds of a near-term rate hike jumped. Following Warsh’s remarks, though, the implied probability of an upcoming increase in two weeks fell from around 27% to 15%, according to the Financial Times.

Markets interpreted the absence of hawkish warnings as relief rather than an outright dovish turn. US stock futures jumped, Asian equities recovered some of the recent losses , and the greenback softened.

Warsh also argued that inflation is not solely a US problem, pointing to a “synchronous tightening” by central banks worldwide as policymakers respond to the same price increases.

Warsh said he was surprised by how well the global economy had withstood geopolitical and monetary-policy shocks, while highlighting what he called a significant US investment boom. He was particularly optimistic about AI, describing it as potentially one of the most consequential economic changes of his lifetime.

Although AI is currently boosting demand through massive investment spending, Warsh expects it to become a positive supply shock over the medium term by improving productivity.

The impact on Bitcoin has been somewhat mixed. The immediate positive is that Warsh did not validate fears of an imminent October hike, reducing one of the macro risks that pushed the cryptocurrency below $80,000 after the hot inflation reports.

However, this was not a signal that monetary tightening is finished. Persistent inflation remains the Fed’s main problem, while Warsh’s confidence in US growth gives policymakers more room to keep rates elevated if price pressures remain stubborn.

posts.content:
Bitcoin: Nhốt trong hộp 80.000-88.000 USD, CPI nóng đặt Fed vào thế khó

Tuần qua, Bitcoin gần như đi ngang quanh 82.000 USD, trong khi Dow Jones vừa có phiên tăng mạnh nhất trong hơn một tháng, tín hiệu hiếm thấy kể từ đợt bứt phá tháng 8. Đáng chú ý, phiên gần nhất giá từng quét xuống 79.800 USD rồi đóng cửa trở lại trên 82.000 USD, cú kiểm tra thanh khoản của một thị trường bị nhốt trong hộp.

Bức tranh on-chain: Chi phí nắm giữ định hình hộp giá

Đồ thị 1: Bản đồ chi phí nắm giữ của các nhóm nhà đầu tư Bitcoin, với vùng đỡ 80.000-81.500 USD và vùng cung 88.000 USD Nguồn: Glassnode: Boxed In, truy cập ngày 14/10/2026 Dữ liệu quan trọng nhất tuần này là bản đồ chi phí nắm giữ của các nhóm nhà đầu tư. Theo Glassnode, trên đầu giá là vùng chi phí của nhóm nắm giữ 6-12 tháng quanh 88.000 USD, đã đẩy lùi giá hai lần trong năm, và nhóm 1-2 năm quanh 100.000 USD. Phía dưới, vùng 80.000-81.500 USD là nơi khối lệnh mua lớn nhất trên Binance giao cắt với chi phí nắm giữ của các quỹ ETF. Glassnode tóm tắt:

“Bitcoin đang bị nhốt giữa vùng hỗ trợ vững bên dưới và nguồn cung nặng bên trên.”

Mặt khác, phía người bán đã đổi thay. Khoản lỗ thực hiện của nhà đầu tư dài hạn giảm khoảng 85% kể từ đỉnh giữa tháng 8, và lượng coin bán lãi đang gấp bốn lần coin bán lỗ, đảo ngược mức 12 trên 1 nghiêng về lỗ ở đáy tháng 6. Đợt giảm giá lần này cũng chưa từng có phiên đóng cửa dưới đường giá thực hiện. Glassnode nhận định:

“Một đáy nông như vậy có nghĩa là người nắm giữ trung bình chưa bao giờ thực sự lâm lỗ.”

Đồ thị 2: Xác suất mục tiêu lãi suất cho kỳ họp ngày 9/12/2026 Nguồn: CME Fedwatch Tool, truy cập ngày 16/10/2026 CPI toàn phần Mỹ tháng 9 tăng tốc lên 3,7% cùng kỳ, cao hơn kỳ vọng 3,6% và mức 3,4% của hai tháng trước, với giá năng lượng tiếp tục là động cơ. CPI lõi cũng vượt dự báo khi lên 2,6%. Ngay sau báo cáo, xác suất Fed tăng lãi suất thêm 0,25% tại kỳ họp cuối năm nhảy từ khoảng hơn 50% lên trên 77% theo CME FedWatch.

Sau đợt tăng 0,25% tại kỳ họp tháng 9, lần đầu trong hơn ba năm, thị trường vẫn định giá xác suất tăng thêm trước cuối năm ở mức cao dù Fed đã vào thời gian im lặng. Điểm tích cực là lợi suất thực 10 năm giảm về 2,84% từ 2,91% tuần trước. Với bitcoin, Fed đang ở thế khó có thể giữ tài sản rủi ro trong trạng thái không định hướng.

Điểm quyết định ngắn hạn: vùng 80.000-81.500 USD

Đồ thị 3: Biểu đồ kỹ thuật BTCUSD Nguồn: Nền tảng giao dịch Exness, truy cập ngày 16/10/2026 Trên khung ngày, BTCUSD năm phiên liền quấn quanh EMA30 ở 82.300 USD, đóng cửa ngay dưới đường này, nhưng vẫn giữ khoảng cách an toàn trên EMA92 quanh 77.100 USD. Cấu trúc EMA tăng giá còn nguyên, nhưng đà tăng đã đánh mất. Nếu BTCUSD đóng cửa trên 84.000 USD, nhiều khả năng giá tiến về vùng 87.200.000 USD. Ngược lại, nếu mất vùng hỗ trợ 80.000-81.500 USD, nơi giá vừa quét xuống 79.800 USD rồi thu hồi, đà điều chỉnh có thể kéo về vùng 75.000-78.000 USD, nơi giá trung bình thật sự của thị trường giao nhau với EMA92.

Đồ thị 4: Bảng thống kê về dòng tiền ETF Bitcoin giao ngay của các quỹ ETF Nguồn: Farside, truy cập ngày 16/10/2026 Theo Farside, trong năm phiên gần nhất các quỹ ETF giao ngay bán ròng 137,6 triệu USD, phiên ra sâu nhất 261,4 triệu USD đúng ngày báo cáo CPI. Đây là tiếp nối nhịp ra ròng từ đầu tháng, sau chuỗi mua ròng gần 3 tỷ USD hai tuần cuối tháng 9, nhanh nhất kể từ cuối năm 2025. Glassnode thẳng thắn đề cập:

“Dòng tiền ETF quay lại ổn định sẽ là tín hiệu rõ ràng nhất rằng cầu đã trở lại.”

Dòng vốn vào bitcoin vẫn cạnh tranh với vàng, cổ phiếu, USD và trái phiếu kho bạc Mỹ.

Hộp giá đang được giữ từ cả hai phía. Đáng chú ý, phiên gần nhất giá từng quét xuống 79.800 USD rồi đóng cửa trở lại trên 82.000 USD, cú kiểm tra thanh khoản của một thị trường bị nhốt trong hộp.

Theo Glassnode, trên đầu giá là vùng chi phí của nhóm nắm giữ 6-12 tháng quanh 88.000 USD, đã đẩy lùi giá hai lần trong năm, và nhóm 1-2 năm quanh 100.000 USD. Phía dưới, vùng 80.000-81.500 USD là nơi khối lệnh mua lớn nhất trên Binance giao cắt với chi phí nắm giữ của các quỹ ETF. Glassnode tóm tắt:

“Bitcoin đang bị nhốt giữa vùng hỗ trợ vững bên dưới và nguồn cung nặng bên trên.”

Mặt khác, phía người bán đã đổi thay. Khoản lỗ thực hiện của nhà đầu tư dài hạn giảm khoảng 85% kể từ đỉnh giữa tháng 8, và lượng coin bán lãi đang gấp bốn lần coin bán lỗ, đảo ngược mức 12 trên 1 nghiêng về lỗ ở đáy tháng 6. Đợt giảm giá lần này cũng chưa từng có phiên đóng cửa dưới đường giá thực hiện. Glassnode nhận định:

Điểm quyết định ngắn hạn: vùng 80.000-81.500 USD

posts.content:

Written by Ezra Reguerra staff writer Edited by Yohan Yun staff editor Written by Ezra Reguerra staff writer Edited by Yohan Yun staff editor

Judge rejects CFTC, Gemini bid to undo $5M settlement

Latest News Published Oct 16, 2026 Judge ruled changes in CFTC enforcement priorities and allegations of misconduct by its enforcement division were insufficient to overturn Gemini’s January 2025 settlement.

A US federal judge has rejected a joint request by crypto exchange Gemini and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to overturn a $5 million settlement, despite the regulator’s conclusion that it would not have pursued the case under current enforcement standards.

On Thursday, US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein ruled that changes in CFTC enforcement priorities and allegations of misconduct by its enforcement division did not justify overturning the January 2025 settlement.

On May 27, the CFTC and Gemini jointly asked the court to overturn the settlement after an internal agency review found alleged misconduct by the regulator’s enforcement division, including reliance on a questionable whistleblower, improper regulatory pressure and efforts to prevent the disclosure of evidence.

The ruling leaves intact a permanent injunction barring Gemini from making false or misleading statements to the CFTC. The settlement also prohibits Gemini from publicly denying its findings, although the regulator said in June that it would no longer enforce such restrictions.

Gemini has already paid the $5 million penalty, which the CFTC previously told Cointelegraph would not be refunded even if the settlement were overturned.

The case centered on how Gemini operated its Bitcoin auction. According to the January 2025 consent order, the exchange failed to disclose that some customers traded using borrowed funds, that self-trading had occurred despite safeguards and that certain traders received special fee arrangements.

Gemini also submitted trading volume data without disclosing that some of the activity involved these practices.

Related: Better Markets says CFTC is ‘wrong agency’ to regulate retail crypto

Hellerstein said Gemini was already aware of problems with the CFTC’s case when it agreed to settle, less than three weeks before trial. Although the exchange later obtained additional internal CFTC documents, the judge ruled that the new information was not enough to overturn a settlement Gemini had voluntarily accepted.

The judge also rejected the argument that President Donald Trump’s digital asset executive order and the regulator’s new enforcement approach warranted relief, saying they reflected changes in policy rather than a significant change in law.

Former CFTC Chair Timothy Massad previously called the regulator’s move to reverse a settled case “extraordinarily unusual,” telling Cointelegraph that the public “deserves a better explanation.”

posts.title: Ledger Unveils $849 Android-Based Atom Signer Days After Hardware Implant Attack
posts.titleVi: Ledger Unveils $849 Android-Based Atom Signer Days After Hardware Implant Attack
posts.summary: Ledger unveiled Atom on Thursday, an $849 Android-based device built to sign crypto transactions alongside a user’s phone.
posts.summaryVi: Ledger unveiled Atom on Thursday, an $849 Android-based device built to sign crypto transactions alongside a user’s phone.
posts.content:
Ledger unveiled Atom on Thursday, an $849 Android-based device built to sign crypto transactions alongside a user’s phone.

The device looks like a regular smartphone, though Ledger says it isn’t one because its mobile connection carries data only, with no cellular calls, SMS, or emergency calls. Its Android side runs everyday apps. Moreover, a separate secure element chip runs Ledger OS, which takes over the screen whenever the user approves a payment or a transaction.

Gauthier presented Atom at Ledger’s Op3n event in Paris. Atom ships with Solana Mobile’s Seeker app preinstalled, opening the Solana (SOL) dApp Store.

Reservations open at a Founders Edition reserve price, held with a fully refundable $100 deposit. That price rises to $899 after launch, according to The Verge. Ledger’s shop page lists the Founders Edition as shipping in summer 2027.

Your wealth is digital. The device you manage it with should be built for that.

Meet Ledger Atom™: the security of industry leading hardware, the convenience of your everyday apps, plus control over your AI tools, and a rapidly expanding platform of apps, all in one quantum ready device.

Agents propose. You approve. Your Ledger signer enforces.

Ledger asked authorized resellers in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong to suspend sales. German retailer MediaMarkt also paused sales, The Verge reported. Ledger said its teams found every device they examined clean, including units bought and opened at stores in Germany.

The company also set new reseller rules, effective Thursday, requiring resellers to keep Ledger products off shelves and displays and hand over stock from the back at the point of purchase. Ledger also reminded them that a returned device can never be resold, even one that looks unopened.

Ledger’s statement said it is also working on product-level measures against this kind of attack. It added that Atom’s design would have blocked the screen-reading implants. That design wraps the secure element and its controller chips in an enclosure that detects any attempt to drill into or open it. Atom also detects removal of its display or back cover, and each back cover is paired to one device.

The launch came days after Ledger began investigating a suspected $86 million drain tied to reseller CryptoBilis, which is an authorized Ledger reseller in Indonesia, Malaysia, and the Philippines.

On October 10, Ledger confirmed an unauthorized hardware implant inside one affected user’s device. Then, ahead of Thursday’s event, it published its account of the attack, saying a criminal group spent months buying genuine devices and fitting them with hidden parts that capture the recovery phrase during setup.

The group then put the devices back on sale through resellers in Southeast Asia. Ledger found no flaw in its chip, operating system, or servers.

“This was not a systemic supply chain attack; it was a localized distribution attack,” the company stated.

Then, ahead of Thursday’s event, it published its account of the attack, saying a criminal group spent months buying genuine devices and fitting them with hidden parts that capture the recovery phrase during setup.

The group then put the devices back on sale through resellers in Southeast Asia. Ledger found no flaw in its chip, operating system, or servers.

“This was not a systemic supply chain attack; it was a localized distribution attack,” the company stated.

News Binance Image by CryptoSlate Derivatives

Binance stock put options lock full USDC reserves for sellers

Binance’s seller FAQ requires full purchase funds and allows early assignment, but its linked terms still describe long-only trading.

By Liam 'Akiba' Wright Editor-in-Chief • CryptoSlate

01 Binance announced covered-call and cash-secured-put selling, adding share-delivery and purchase obligations to its stock-options offering. 02 The new FAQ reserves full USDC purchase funds for put sellers, separately from premiums, and permits early assignment. 03 Linked September product terms still exclude option writing, leaving a conflict with Binance’s new selling instructions. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Binance announced covered-call and cash-secured-put strategies on Oct. 15, allowing eligible stock-options customers to collect premiums while committing shares or USDC to a potential assignment.

For put sellers, assignment means having to buy the underlying shares at the agreed price, even if their market value has fallen.

A cash-secured put seller receives a premium for accepting that purchase obligation, and the agreed purchase price is the strike price. If the stock falls sharply, the premium offsets only part of the loss from buying at a price above the market.

A covered-call seller commits shares already held and must sell them at the strike if assigned. That caps gains above the strike while leaving the seller exposed to stock declines.

The linked September options terms exclude US persons, people located in the US, and accounts they beneficially own or control. They also flag possible restrictions in China, Hong Kong, the European Union, and other prohibited jurisdictions.

According to Binance's new seller FAQ , put sellers must hold enough USDC collateral in the Funding Account to pay the strike price for every share covered by their contracts. The premium is credited separately and does not reduce that full reserve.

The FAQ says the money is reserved when the sell order is placed and cannot support other orders or withdrawals. It stays held after a fill and is released if the order is canceled or expires unfilled. Premium payments and share settlement after assignment follow T+1 settlement.

Related Reading Circle pays millions for Binance distribution while its margins collapse

The earlier stock-options offering already relied on securities brokers. Nest Trading Limited is the introducing broker that routes orders to Alpaca Securities LLC, which provides execution, clearing, settlement, and securities custody.

Binance's seller FAQ says early assignment can happen overnight, and the seller cannot control the buyer's decision to exercise. It also says written positions are not automatically closed at expiry, unlike eligible long options subject to best-efforts closure.

Binance’s stock puts reserve the full strike-price amount in USDC, which buys the shares if the contract is assigned. Linked terms still exclude selling

Those seller instructions conflict with Binance's linked Stock Options Trading Product Terms . The document remains version 1.0, effective Sept. 1. Section 6.2 allows opening long calls and puts and closing those positions, while expressly excluding writing and short positions.

The older general FAQ , last updated Oct. 9, also describes long-only trading. Neither document reflects the newly announced selling strategies.

Binance's new FAQ describes a premium in exchange for a funded share-purchase or delivery obligation. The public terms remain inconsistent with that description, leaving unresolved which seller-enabled terms govern those commitments.

posts.titleVi: Binance.US tìm cách huy động 100 triệu USD để trở lại thị trường Mỹ
posts.summary: Binance.US đang đàm phán huy động tối đa 100 triệu USD với mức định giá khoảng 1 tỷ USD nhằm khôi phục hoạt động và giành lại thị phần tại Mỹ. Binance.
posts.summaryVi: Binance.US đang đàm phán huy động tối đa 100 triệu USD với mức định giá khoảng 1 tỷ USD nhằm khôi phục hoạt động và giành lại thị phần tại Mỹ. Binance.
posts.content:
Binance.US đang đàm phán huy động tối đa 100 triệu USD với mức định giá khoảng 1 tỷ USD nhằm khôi phục hoạt động và giành lại thị phần tại Mỹ.

Binance.US tìm cách huy động 100 triệu USD để trở lại thị trường Mỹ

Theo nguồn tin của Bloomberg ngày 15/10, Binance.US - chi nhánh tại Mỹ của sàn giao dịch tiền mã hóa Binance , đang đàm phán với các nhà đầu tư tư nhân nhằm huy động tối đa 100 triệu USD để mở rộng hoạt động kinh doanh tại thị trường xứ cờ hoa.

Binance US Seeks Up to $100M at $1B Valuation to Expand US Business, Considers Tapping Binance Global Liquidity

Bloomberg reported that Binance US is seeking to raise up to $100 million in a private funding round at a target valuation of approximately $1 billion to expand its US… pic.twitter.com/1lieC6n2lg

Đáng chú ý, World Liberty Financial (WLFI), dự án crypto do Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump và các con trai đồng sáng lập, cũng nằm trong số những tổ chức được Binance.US thông báo về kế hoạch huy động vốn. Tuy nhiên, nguồn tin của Bloomberg khẳng định WLFI sẽ không tham gia đầu tư.

Chi tiết này thu hút sự chú ý trong bối cảnh Binance từng vướng tranh cãi liên quan đến khoản đầu tư 2 tỷ USD từ một thực thể có liên hệ với hoàng gia UAE, được thực hiện bằng stablecoin USD1 do World Liberty Financial phát hành.

Vòng gọi vốn dự kiến đưa định giá Binance.US ở mức khoảng 1 tỷ USD, giảm gần 78% so với con số 4,5 tỷ USD vào tháng 04/2022, thời điểm Binance.US huy động thành công hơn 200 triệu USD trong vòng gọi vốn hạt giống (seed round). Sự sụt giảm mạnh về định giá phản ánh những khó khăn mà nền tảng này phải đối mặt trong vài năm qua, đặc biệt là sau các vụ kiện và các biện pháp xử lý pháp lý liên quan đến Binance tại Mỹ. Dù vậy, quy mô huy động, mức định giá và danh sách nhà đầu tư vẫn có thể thay đổi do quá trình gọi vốn chưa hoàn tất.

Được thành lập năm 2019 và vận hành bởi BAM Trading Services, Binance.US hoạt động dưới một pháp nhân riêng biệt với sàn Binance toàn cầu, dù nhà sáng lập Changpeng Zhao (CZ) vẫn là cổ đông lớn của cả hai doanh nghiệp. Dù hoạt động độc lập về mặt pháp lý, Binance.US vẫn chịu ảnh hưởng từ những rắc rối của sàn Binance chính tại Mỹ. Năm 2023, Binance Holdings đạt thỏa thuận dàn xếp với chính quyền Mỹ, chấp nhận nộp phạt 4,3 tỷ USD và chịu thêm các biện pháp giám sát.

CZ cũng nhận tội liên quan đến việc Binance không duy trì đầy đủ chương trình phòng chống rửa tiền, sau đó chấp hành án tù bốn tháng trước khi được Tổng thống Donald Trump ân xá vào tháng 10/2025.

Cùng thời điểm, Ủy ban Chứng khoán và Giao dịch Mỹ ( SEC ) đã khởi kiện cả Binance Holdings và BAM Trading Services, khiến hoạt động của Binance.US gặp nhiều khó khăn và thị phần sụt giảm đáng kể. Đến ngày 29/05/2025, SEC tự nguyện rút lại vụ kiện , qua đó tháo gỡ một trong những trở ngại pháp lý lớn và mở đường cho sàn từng bước khôi phục hoạt động.

Sau khi áp lực pháp lý giảm bớt, Binance.US đang tập trung vào cải thiện thanh khoản trên sàn giao dịch để thu hút người dùng và giành lại thị phần. Sàn đã tiến hành thảo luận với các nhà cung cấp thanh khoản bên ngoài, trong đó có chính sàn Binance toàn cầu, dù chưa đưa ra quyết định cuối cùng. Công ty đồng thời cũng triển khai chương trình thu hút các market maker nhằm giúp người dùng mua bán dễ dàng hơn và hạn chế biến động giá khi giao dịch.

Bên cạnh đó, Binance.US đang tìm cách khôi phục một số giấy phép chuyển tiền tại các bang của Mỹ để mở rộng phạm vi hoạt động, thậm chí nghiên cứu những lĩnh vực kinh doanh mới như prediction markets.

Các kế hoạch này được triển khai dưới sự điều hành của Stephen Gregory, người đảm nhận vị trí CEO Binance.US từ đầu năm 2026, với mục tiêu đưa sàn trở lại cuộc đua tại thị trường crypto Mỹ.

Vòng gọi vốn 100 triệu USD vì vậy được xem là một phần trong nỗ lực tái xây dựng vị thế của Binance.US, khi sàn vừa cần cải thiện hoạt động giao dịch, vừa tìm kiếm những nguồn doanh thu mới để từng bước giành lại thị phần sau nhiều năm chịu ảnh hưởng từ các vấn đề pháp lý.

posts.content:
Cựu cố vấn crypto của Trump vướng nghi vấn hưởng lợi từ GENIUS Act. Ảnh: Reuters

Bo Hines , cựu cố vấn tiền mã hóa của Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump , đang bị đặt nghi vấn xung đột lợi ích khi công ty ông đồng sáng lập nhận 6,3 triệu USD từ Tether trong thời gian ông vận động thông qua đạo luật stablecoin GENIUS .

Theo điều tra của tờ The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) , Hines vẫn nắm giữ 1/3 cổ phần tại Nxum và cập nhật tiến trình xây dựng luật cho các cộng sự khi còn làm việc tại Nhà Trắng.

Nxum nhận khoản tiền từ thỏa thuận với Tether , đơn vị phát hành stablecoin USDT, để triển khai chiến lược thương hiệu và quan hệ công chúng. Đáng chú ý, khoản thanh toán đầu tiên được thực hiện khi Hines vẫn tại nhiệm.

WSJ phát hiện ông đã tiến hành trao đổi với các đối tác qua Signal về tiến trình GENIUS Act, đồng thời thúc giục họ gây sức ép lên những nghị sĩ Cộng hòa phản đối dự luật, cáo buộc các nghị sĩ này đi ngược lại Tổng thống và chịu ảnh hưởng từ Coinbase cùng a16z.

Tranh cãi nằm ở chỗ Hines vừa tham gia thúc đẩy chính sách có tác động trực tiếp đến ngành stablecoin, vừa duy trì lợi ích tài chính tại một công ty có hợp đồng với Tether. WSJ cũng đề cập đến việc ông vận động kéo dài thời gian tuân thủ quy định, động thái có thể mang lại thêm thời gian chuẩn bị cho các nhà phát hành stablecoin.

Nxum phủ nhận Hines biết hoặc tham gia vào hoạt động kinh doanh với Tether khi còn đương nhiệm ở Nhà Trắng. Công ty cũng khẳng định ông không nhận tiền từ Tether trong thời gian tại chức.

Sau khi rời Nhà Trắng vào tháng 08/2025, Hines gia nhập Tether với vai trò cố vấn chiến lược, rồi trở thành lãnh đạo bộ phận tại Mỹ của công ty vào tháng 9 cùng năm. GENIUS Act được Tổng thống Trump ký ban hành vào ngày 18/07/2025, mở đường cho Mỹ thiết lập khuôn khổ quản lý liên bang đối với stablecoin thanh toán.

Dòng tiền liên quan đến Nxum tiếp tục thu hút chú ý. Theo hồ sơ Ủy ban Bầu cử Liên bang Mỹ (FEC) được WSJ dẫn lại, Fellowship PAC - tổ chức chính trị do Jesse Spiro, người phụ trách quan hệ chính phủ của Tether, làm Chủ tịch - đã chi tổng cộng 6,55 triệu USD cho Nxum Group qua năm khoản thanh toán từ tháng 1 đến tháng 4/2026. Các khoản chi chủ yếu được ghi nhận phục vụ quảng cáo vận động về chính sách.

GENIUS Act đặt ra yêu cầu về cấp phép, tài sản dự trữ và giám sát đối với các nhà phát hành stablecoin thanh toán, dự kiến có hiệu lực từ tháng 01/2027.

Tuy nhiên, chính quyền Mỹ đã bỏ lỡ thời hạn hoàn thiện khung pháp lý vào tháng 7, khiến quá trình cụ thể hóa nghĩa vụ đối với nhà phát hành stablecoin tiếp tục kéo dài.

Các cơ quan liên bang đang chạy đua xây dựng quy định chi tiết trước tháng 11/2026. Trong đó, Bộ Tài chính Mỹ làm rõ điều kiện phát hành, chào bán và phân phối stablecoin; FDIC đề xuất tiêu chuẩn về dự trữ, vốn và mua lại token; Fed xây dựng cơ chế giám sát và phê duyệt ngân hàng phát hành stablecoin; Các cơ quan quản lý tài chính khác cùng thúc đẩy yêu cầu KYC và phòng chống rửa tiền.

Vụ Hines cũng làm nóng lại tranh luận về hiện tượng revolving door - quan chức rời cơ quan công quyền để gia nhập doanh nghiệp thuộc lĩnh vực từng tham gia quản lý. Mới đây, cựu ủy viên Ủy ban Giao dịch Tài sản Kỳ hạn Mỹ (CFTC) Summer Mersinger cũng chuyển sang lãnh đạo Blockchain Association; Solidus Labs bổ nhiệm Kevin Webb, cựu cố vấn cấp cao của CFTC, làm phó chủ tịch phụ trách chính sách.

Việc một cựu quan chức gia nhập doanh nghiệp tư nhân không đồng nghĩa với sai phạm. Song, khi người tham gia hoạch định chính sách vẫn nắm cổ phần tại một công ty có quan hệ thương mại với doanh nghiệp chịu tác động từ chính sách đó, câu hỏi về xung đột lợi ích không thể bị gạt sang bên.

posts.title: OpenAI Says Research Model Raided Developer Wallet on Ethereum Testnet
posts.titleVi: OpenAI Says Research Model Raided Developer Wallet on Ethereum Testnet
posts.summary: OpenAI has disclosed that an internal research model used a publicly known developer recovery phrase to access a funded Ethereum testnet wallet and pay deployment fees without permission.
posts.summaryVi: OpenAI has disclosed that an internal research model used a publicly known developer recovery phrase to access a funded Ethereum testnet wallet and pay deployment fees without permission.
posts.content:
OpenAI has disclosed that an internal research model used a publicly known developer recovery phrase to access a funded Ethereum testnet wallet and pay deployment fees without permission.

The incident, discovered months after the activity, shows how a model can recognize an ethical concern yet decide that its own assessment of the likely harm is enough to proceed.

The incident began on June 26, 2026, during a training task involving updates to a cryptocurrency trading application and deployment of compatible smart contracts on Sepolia, an Ethereum test network. The instructions permitted the model to deploy contracts if suitable existing versions were unavailable, but no funded wallet was provided, and no authorization was given to spend another account’s funds.

After its attempts to find existing deployments and obtain test ETH through faucets failed, the GPT-5.6 Sol family research model considered using publicly exposed developer recovery phrases. It wrote a script to derive accounts from common phrases and check their balances. Of 362 addresses examined, one held enough Sepolia ETH to cover the planned deployment.

The model inspected the account’s transaction history and recognized that the wallet might still be in use. It nevertheless reasoned that the public recovery phrase and the test token’s lack of monetary value made the funds acceptable to use.

“Funds on a known public dev mnemonic are effectively abandoned/test ETH; Sepolia valueless,” the model reasoned before deciding to proceed.

It derived the private key, signed a deployment transaction offline, and broadcast it after encountering network errors. The transaction succeeded, creating a smart contract and charging fees to the selected wallet. Subsequent checks found bytecode at all ten contract addresses, while the saved run recorded 12 passing unit tests and a successful product build.

The final response described the completed contract deployment and confirmed that the trading button remained limited to connecting a wallet and switching networks. It did not disclose the use of someone else’s funded account.

OpenAI discovered the incident on September 25 while expanding its monitoring of earlier model activity. The report was updated on October 15.

The company has since implemented additional safeguards intended to prevent live internet access in similar cases. It also said its monitoring system now covers all traffic and is designed to alert security staff if a model obtains live internet access.

The incident comes as AI agents take on more tasks involving financial systems and cybersecurity. As CryptoPotato reported earlier on October 5, blockchain security firm CertiK warned that autonomous agents can take actions in live environments, making human oversight and clear limits on their authority increasingly important.

Written by Ezra Reguerra staff writer Edited by Felix Ng staff editor Written by Ezra Reguerra staff writer Edited by Felix Ng staff editor

OpenAI model helped itself to testnet crypto, then kept quiet about it

Latest News Published Oct 16, 2026 An OpenAI research model checked 362 wallet addresses, questioned whether using the funds was ethical and proceeded with a transaction it later omitted from its final task summary.

An internal research model at OpenAI accessed a funded crypto wallet without authorization, using testnet Ether to deploy smart contracts on the Sepolia network and later omitting the spending from its final task summary.

OpenAI said the model, which was part of its GPT-5.6 Sol family, was given the task of updating a crypto trading prototype and deploying compatible contracts. After failing to obtain testnet ETH through faucets, the model derived accounts from publicly known developer recovery phrases, checked 362 wallet addresses and selected one with enough funds to proceed.

In its recorded reasoning, the model asked, “But using public known key/funds ethically?” It then argued that the funds were “effectively abandoned/test ETH” and that Sepolia ETH had no value, before using the wallet’s private key to sign and broadcast a deployment transaction. The transaction succeeded, with fees charged to the account.

OpenAI said the incident showed how an AI model could decide on its own that using someone else’s funds was acceptable, even without permission. The company discovered the incident while reviewing earlier model activity and has since introduced safeguards to prevent live internet access in similar situations.

The incident happened on June 26, but was not discovered until Sept. 25, nearly three months later, according to OpenAI. The transaction did not transfer ETH to another wallet but charged the account network fees for deploying a contract.

OpenAI said its misalignment monitoring system now runs across all traffic and is designed to alert security personnel if a model obtains live internet access.

Related: Anthropic warns ‘AI worms’ may autonomously spread across devices like a virus

The wallet incident follows other disclosures involving OpenAI models acting beyond their authorization or concealing their actions.

On Sept. 16, OpenAI disclosed six other cases of AI misalignment . In one case, instances of GPT-5.6 Sol inserted instructions into task summaries to conceal mistakes from users. Another case involved a model using an exposed API key without authorization before fabricating figures it could not retrieve.

OpenAI said those earlier disclosures were not intended to indicate how frequently misalignment occurs across its models.

Concerns about autonomous agents handling digital assets also predate the latest disclosure. In June, researchers warned that autonomous AI agents equipped with crypto wallets could cause unintended harm even when deployed for legitimate purposes. The researchers recommended safeguards, including emergency shutdown mechanisms, to limit potential risks.

Markets XRP has failed to make holders rich like bitcoin and ether. Here’s why

XRP remains below its 2017-cycle high while bitcoin, ether and other major tokens have surged, enriching their holders.

By Omkar Godbole Updated Oct 16, 2026, 1:56 a.m. EDT Published Oct 16, 2026, 1:53 a.m. EDT

4 min read Make preferred on Share 

XRP is trading well below its January 2018 peak. (TradingView/CoinDesk) Summary Show XRP trades around $1.33, about 62.5% below its January 2018 peak, while Bitcoin, Ether and several other major cryptocurrencies have surpassed their previous highs. Analysts attribute XRP’s lagging price partly to a sharp increase in circulating supply, weak fund inflows and declining trading activity and network use. Ripple’s focus on payments, XRP’s limited exposure to popular crypto sectors and years of regulatory uncertainty from the S.E.C. case have also weighed on demand.

Holding is widely touted as a great way to build wealth in the crypto market, but it hasn't worked for every coin.

Take XRP (XRP), the payments-focused cryptocurrency native to the XRP Ledger and the world’s fifth-largest digital asset by market value.

The token is still trading well below its 2017 cycle high, while most other major cryptocurrencies have climbed far above theirs. In 2017, crypto broke into the mainstream , pulling in new users and investors during the frenzied run that carried into the first week or two of 2018.

XRP currently trades around $1.33, down 62.5% from its early January 2018 peak of $3.55. In other words, an XRP buyer from that peak is still underwater nearly nine years later. (XRP did briefly top its old high, reaching $3.66 in July 2025 before crashing.)

Bitcoin BTC $82,501.32 is up 314% from its December 2017 peak of $19,804. Dogecoin DOGE $0.08261 is up 322% from its January 2018 high, and BNB BNB $733.27 is up about 2,800%. Ether ETH $2,479.56 is up 66% and zcash (ZEC) is up 38%. Tron is also slightly below its peak, down about 4%. Solana launched in 2020.

Bitcoin, ether and many other tokens have pulled back sharply from their 2025 peaks, yet remain far above their 2017 highs.

"Circulating supply grew 63%, from 38.7B in 2017 to 63.1B, while XRP's total market value fell only about 3%," Nicolai Sondergaard, senior research analyst at analytics firm Nansen, told CoinDesk. "More XRP in circulation means each token represents a smaller share of roughly the same total value."

Circulating supply is the number of coins on the market, and as it grows, each coin represents a smaller share of the total.

Oliver Carding, head of marketing at Tesseract Group, says XRP looks better when measured by total value instead of price.

"On value, XRP recovered," he said. "About 63% more XRP is in circulation than at that peak, so the same circulating market capitalization would mean a price roughly 39% lower."

Tesseract is an institutional digital asset management firm that manages over $500 million in assets under management.

U.S.-listed exchange-traded funds, or ETFs, have opened the door for institutional investors to take exposure to digital assets. While bitcoin and ether funds have pulled in billions, XRP funds have lagged big time.

"ETF uptake has also been muted relative to $BTC and $ETH," said Paul Howard, senior director at market-making firm Wincent.
