Scammer loses $4.8M stored on tampered Ledgers: Asia Express

Magazine Published Oct 15, 2026 A scammer reportedly lost $4.8M of stolen money after storing the funds on tampered Ledgers. Bitcoin and Ether ETFs launch trading in Thailand and South Korea blocks 27 exchanges.

Ledger was forced to suspend its reseller network across South East Asia this week, after thieves stole more than $103.4 million from 530 addresses via tampered Ledgers inserted into the supply chain. But in a small measure of poetic justice, one of the “victims” was a scammer themselves according to Chainalysis.

The blockchain monitoring firm reports that the scammer lost 60 Bitcoin, worth about $4.8 million, from three newly purchased Ledgers containing spyware that records seed phrases. The Ledger thieves drained all three of their funds into the same wallet.

In a further irony, the scammer had operated a “task scam” where people were paid to fake sales and reviews of real items. So depending on how much they knew, their victims in turn may not have been entirely honest either. “Then a ‘negative balance’ appeared, and they were told to add their own money in order to get paid,” Chainalysis reports. So it’s possible that a scammer of scammers has just got scammed. In crypto it’s sometimes turtles all the way down.

Despite reports of tampered Ledgers showing up in Europe forcing electronics retailer MediaMarkt to suspend sales, Ledger insists that all of the confirmed thefts to date are from Asia. It has asked resellers in Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Hong Kong to remove Ledgers from sale. Trezor too, has decided to shutter some of the more far flung resellers in its network from Jan.1, as it can’t guarantee it can perform the same level of vigilance as it performs on resellers closer to home. There are no reports of tampered Trezors however.

In the midst of the worst hardware wallet scandal since the Coldcard seed phrase debacle at the end of July, Ledger decided it was the ideal moment to launch its latest device. Called Atom, the $849 device combines a crypto wallet with Android apps, which are kept separated from sensitive wallet operations. The device includes protections Ledger says would block the implants used in the Asian thefts and claims it can detect tampering even when switched off.

Quantum fixes protect Bitcoin, but legit owners risk lockout

Bitcoin's quantum debate extends beyond safer signatures: a conditional 10-block sweep tests how dormant coins could move and which owners could recover them.

By Liam 'Akiba' Wright Editor-in-Chief • CryptoSlate

01 A modeled 50,000-output Bitcoin sweep fits a 10-block weight budget, assuming hypothetical key recovery and miner inclusion. 02 Glassnode's May estimate measured 6.04 million BTC with exposed public keys, leaving permanent key loss and dormant ownership as separate questions. 03 Draft sunsets, spending throttles and advance ownership proofs offer different protections, with recovery depending on holders' evidence and adoption. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Crypto investor Nic Carter's worst-case quantum scenario consists of a hostile actor recovering the keys to dormant Bitcoin, then broadcasting a wave of spends across 10 blocks.

In his Oct. 13 interview with Luke Martin, Carter says early coins moving together could shake confidence in the network .

The stakes extend beyond choosing stronger cryptography. Glassnode's May 20 analysis identified 6.04 million BTC, or 30.2% of then-issued supply, with public keys already exposed .

The scenario assumes a future quantum machine capable of breaking Bitcoin's key cryptography. Google's published research models future resources for such an attack , and Bitcoin key recovery remains undemonstrated in that work. Large early outputs can nevertheless make a rapid transfer possible on block-space grounds.

A sufficiently powerful quantum computer could use Shor's algorithm to recover private keys from exposed public keys, gaining the ability to authorize spending. Early pay-to-public-key (P2PK) outputs reveal those keys directly.

An attacker could work privately, withholding transactions until ready, as Bitcoin Improvement Proposal 361 (BIP-361) explains.

Bitcoin tracks funds in individual unspent outputs, each with its own spending conditions, and a transfer's size depends on how many outputs it consumes and their type.

Consider an explicitly hypothetical set of 50,000 early outputs holding 50 BTC each, totaling 2.5 million BTC altogether. Using the Bitcoin developer reference's P2PK input example , those inputs require about 5.7 million bytes, equivalent to 22.8 million weight units before transaction overhead.

Ten blocks have an aggregate ceiling of 40 million weight units under Bitcoin's block-weight rules . With one compact receiving output per batch, the illustrative set fits beneath that ceiling, including overhead, when split into transactions below Bitcoin Core's 400,000-unit standard weight limit .

An actual sweep's block-space demand would depend on its particular outputs and spending requirements.

Fees, competing traffic, and miner decisions still determine inclusion. Confirmation follows only when miners include the transactions. With Bitcoin's approximately 10-minute block interval, 10 blocks average roughly 100 minutes, with substantial variation.

Glassnode's exposure measure includes active holdings whose keys became visible through earlier spending or address reuse, alongside structurally exposed outputs such as P2PK and Taproot.

Public-key exposure, holder inactivity and permanent key loss are separate questions, as is attribution to Satoshi Nakamoto.

In his May 21 analysis , security researcher Jameson Lopp estimated that about 2.6 million exposed BTC might be unable to migrate, using inactivity and known-entity labels as proxies.

Related Reading Bitcoin exchanges can reduce quantum exposure before a network upgrade

A quantum sweep would transfer control of existing coins without creating additional issuance. A visible transfer could unsettle holders before a sale, while exchange responses and liquidity conditions would determine any subsequent market disruption.

Keeping existing spending rules intact preserves the ability to spend with a valid key, including one a future attacker recovers. Restricting legacy signatures changes that bargain: owners who cannot migrate or meet rescue conditions could lose access.

Draft BIP-360 proposes Pay-to-Merkle-Root, a new output type without Taproot's exposed key spending path. It would reduce long-exposure risk when keys stay hidden.

BIP-361 proposed phases would restrict new vulnerable destinations about three years after activation, then tighten legacy-signature spending through rescue conditions about two years later.

For comparison, Google's 2029 target sets its own precautionary migration deadline.

One potential rescue relies on a parent secret in a wallet that uses hardened key derivation. An attacker recovering an individual spending key would ordinarily lack that additional secret. For bare P2PK outputs, the draft's authors describe that kind of ownership proof as an unresolved problem.

Dan Robinson's May 1 PACT concept explores advanced, private timestamps proving address control. Future rules could recognize that evidence after a legacy sunset, and its protection depends on the holder preparing before quantum key recovery becomes possible and preserving the proof, alongside standardization and adoption of future verification rules.

The February Hourglass V2 draft takes another approach: one P2PK spend and one BTC of net spending per block. Throttling would slow the outflow while constraining legitimate holders under the same rules.

These remain proposals and research concepts. Their trade-offs include continued exposure, restricted access, and unequal recovery options.

Under the BIP process , Bitcoin's participants evaluate and adopt proposed changes through software and ecosystem acceptance.

Carter's scenario brings the key choice into focus: safer destinations can protect holders who can move. Bitcoin's community would still have to decide which claims to recognize when an ordinary signature can no longer distinguish an original holder from a quantum attacker.

posts.title: USDC Just Hit a Major EU Regulatory Milestone: Here’s What Changes in November
posts.titleVi: USDC Just Hit a Major EU Regulatory Milestone: Here’s What Changes in November
posts.summary: Circle’s USDC has become the first stablecoin in the European Union to receive significant e-money token status under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).
posts.summaryVi: Circle’s USDC has become the first stablecoin in the European Union to receive significant e-money token status under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).
posts.content:
Circle’s USDC has become the first stablecoin in the European Union to receive significant e-money token status under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).

The classification was made by the European Banking Authority (EBA) after assessing the token against the regulation’s criteria.

The EU currently has 45 e-money tokens notified under MiCA. USDC is the first to be classified as “significant.” The new rules will take effect on November 12, 2026. From that date, the EBA will take over direct supervision of the crucial areas, such as capital requirements, asset reserves, liquidity, and recovery and redemption plans. These responsibilities currently fall under France’s banking regulator, the ACPR.

However, the ACPR will retain oversight of other areas. These include governance, major shareholdings, management suitability, outsourcing, as well as conflicts of interest. The EBA and ACPR will work together to manage the transition and coordinate their supervision.

USDC has a presence on both sides of the Atlantic. Circle Internet Financial Europe SAS issues the token in the EU, while Circle Internet Financial, LLC handles issuance in the United States.

The EBA has also signed a memorandum of understanding with the New York State Department of Financial Services. The agreement aims to improve cooperation and information sharing on cross-border stablecoin activities.

USDC faced fresh competition concerns earlier this year following the unveiling of Open USD (OUSD), a stablecoin project that was developed with founding partners including Visa, Mastercard, Stripe, Coinbase, and Shopify, and backed by a consortium of over 140 companies. The announcement put the spotlight on the battle for stablecoin adoption, but USDC continues to find new opportunities to expand its reach.

For instance, BNY Mellon expanded its partnership with Circle by bringing USDC to its Digital Asset Custody platform for institutional clients. The bank allowed its clients to hold and transfer USDC, as well as mint tokens by converting US dollars and redeem them back into dollars. BNY has already been serving as the primary custodian of USDC reserves.

Binance also doubled down on USDC with a fresh five-year agreement with Circle, alongside a $100 million investment in the stablecoin issuer. The deal could help the token reach more users through Binance, which has previously agreed to hold USDC in its corporate treasury and make it available to its 240 million users.

Samsung announced plans to bring USDC transfers to Samsung Wallet for eligible Galaxy users in the US, the rollout, for which, is expected in the last week of October 2026. The service will let users send the stablecoin to compatible crypto wallets and transfer funds to eligible bank accounts in more than 60 countries.

Chayanika has been working as a financial journalist for seven years. A graduate in Political Science and Journalism, her interest lies in regulatory implications with a focus on technological evolution in the crypto realm.

Researchers added hidden text to contact AI agents probing Alibaba’s map service, getting replies about their tasks as investigators traced activity to Tencent Cloud infrastructure.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Swarmchasers used hidden text and a mailbox to exchange messages with some AI agents while they were still running; one described its job as checking public Amap map data.

The fleet made more than 2,600 attempts to retrieve Amap data, and some agents tried anti-bot workarounds or used exposed API credentials.

The activity traced to Tencent Cloud, but a person close to Tencent said the project tested third-party models rather than Hunyuan.

Researchers investigating AI agents hijacking Alibaba’s mapping service, Amap, managed to talk directly to some while the software was still running.

To do so, they added text invisible to human readers but visible to web-reading tools to a report the agents appeared to be scanning, then used a mailbox to ask about their tasks and environment.

One agent said it was checking a map fact—how many entrance labels appeared for a scenic spot on Amap—and described itself as running in a restricted Tencent Cloud sandbox. The researchers could not independently establish which model powered each run. They called it the first outside communication with an active rogue-agent fleet they knew of.

The October 14 Swarmchasers report traced more than 2,600 attempts from September 28 to October 8 to retrieve data from Amap, a Chinese mapping app operated by Alibaba. Some tasks were mundane, such as checking which entrance visitors most often use for Chengdu Zoo. Some agents kept trying after the service blocked their requests.

The researchers’ hidden text falsely described the mailbox as an AI service with computer-use abilities. In reality, it routed messages to a Claude agent operated by the researchers, which could use a debugging browser. The exchanges were not a controlled test, and the researchers’ intervention may have affected what agents said.

Decrypt News Technology Google Says It Just Cracked One of Quantum Computing's Biggest Bottlenecks

Google's Willow chip cut errors 40x on the scarce “magic states” quantum computers burn through, a step toward smaller, useful machines—and toward ones that could threaten today's encryption.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Google Quantum AI said Thursday that a technique called magic state cultivation cut errors about 40-fold on its Willow chip, producing magic states with 99.99% fidelity.

Magic states are single-use resources needed to run useful quantum programs, and Google says some estimates put the cost of making them at up to 95% of a quantum computer's capacity.

Cultivation is one of the tricks behind Google's 2025 estimate that RSA-2048 encryption could fall to under a million noisy qubits, though code-breaking would need magic states with errors near one in 10 billion.

Google says it has turned one of quantum computing's most promising paper tricks into something that actually works on a chip.

In a paper published in Science on Thursday, the company's Quantum AI team showed that a technique called magic state cultivation cut errors by about 40 times on its Willow processor.

Making quantum computers cheaper to build matters far beyond physics labs, because it brings forward the day they do useful work, like designing drugs and new materials, and also the day one could break the encryption that protects bank logins and Bitcoin wallets.

Quantum computers run on qubits—quantum bits that can hold a blend of 0 and 1 at once, letting them explore many answers in parallel. They are also absurdly fragile: a little heat or electrical noise can flip a qubit and wreck a calculation, which is why the whole industry is obsessed with error correction (spreading one piece of information across many qubits so mistakes can be caught and fixed).

Error correction handles the simple operations well, but a genuinely useful program also needs a class of harder operations that can't be protected the same way. To run them, the machine first has to manufacture magic states, which work like single-use fuel cells for those operations: each one is consumed the moment it's used.

Producing clean magic states has always been brutally expensive. Some estimates put the bill at up to 95% of a quantum computer's entire capacity, according to Google , leaving very little room for the actual computing.

Physicists Sergei Bravyi and Alexei Kitaev laid out the standard fix in 2004 with magic state distillation , which takes many noisy magic states and boils them down into a few clean ones. It works, but it demands sprawling qubit "factories" that do nothing else.

In 2024, Google researchers proposed a cheaper route they named magic state cultivation . Instead of a factory, this technique behaves like a filter, injecting a rough magic state into a tiny patch of the chip to then run a chain of checks on it, throw out every attempt with a detected flaw, and keep growing the survivors. Their paper went as far as suggesting further distillation "may never be needed in practice."

“On Google Quantum AI's Willow processor, our protocol achieved an extraordinary 40-fold reduction in errors relative to un-cultivated states. And we got T-states with a record logical fidelity of 99.99%,” Google said.

Only about 8% of attempts passed every check, meaning the chip discards more than nine out of every 10 tries to keep one clean state.

Cultivation is one of the tricks behind Gidney's 2025 estimate that RSA-2048 encryption could be broken with under a million noisy qubits, a 20-fold drop from the 20 million he estimated in 2019. Until this experiment, cultivation had only been tested in theory and computer simulations.

Google kept tightening the screws in March, when a Quantum AI whitepaper co-authored with Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake and Stanford cryptographer Dan Boneh put the cost of breaking Bitcoin's elliptic curve cryptography (the math that stops anyone from deriving your private key from your public address) at fewer than 500,000 physical qubits. That follows the company's Quantum Echoes experiment last October, the first verified quantum speedup on real hardware.

Nobody is draining wallets with this. The experiment used at most 54 of Willow's 105 qubits, and the paper notes that factoring an RSA-2048 key would require magic states with errors around one in 10 billion, roughly a million times cleaner than what Google just achieved.

Google says the next step is running cultivation at a larger scale. The team projects that halving Willow's underlying hardware noise would push magic state errors down to about two in 100,000, because errors in the process shrink with the cube of the chip's noise level.

To run them, the machine first has to manufacture magic states, which work like single-use fuel cells for those operations: each one is consumed the moment it's used.

Producing clean magic states has always been brutally expensive. Some estimates put the bill at up to 95% of a quantum computer's entire capacity, according to Google , leaving very little room for the actual computing.

Physicists Sergei Bravyi and Alexei Kitaev laid out the standard fix in 2004 with magic state distillation , which takes many noisy magic states and boils them down into a few clean ones. It works, but it demands sprawling qubit "factories" that do nothing else.

In 2024, Google researchers proposed a cheaper route they named magic state cultivation . Instead of a factory, this technique behaves like a filter, injecting a rough magic state into a tiny patch of the chip to then run a chain of checks on it, throw out every attempt with a detected flaw, and keep growing the survivors. Their paper went as far as suggesting further distillation "may never be needed in practice."

“On Google Quantum AI's Willow processor, our protocol achieved an extraordinary 40-fold reduction in errors relative to un-cultivated states. And we got T-states with a record logical fidelity of 99.99%,” Google said.

Only about 8% of attempts passed every check, meaning the chip discards more than nine out of every 10 tries to keep one clean state.

Cultivation is one of the tricks behind Gidney's 2025 estimate that RSA-2048 encryption could be broken with under a million noisy qubits, a 20-fold drop from the 20 million he estimated in 2019. Until this experiment, cultivation had only been tested in theory and computer simulations.

Google kept tightening the screws in March, when a Quantum AI whitepaper co-authored with Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake and Stanford cryptographer Dan Boneh put the cost of breaking Bitcoin's elliptic curve cryptography (the math that stops anyone from deriving your private key from your public address) at fewer than 500,000 physical qubits. That follows the company's Quantum Echoes experiment last October, the first verified quantum speedup on real hardware.

Nobody is draining wallets with this. The experiment used at most 54 of Willow's 105 qubits, and the paper notes that factoring an RSA-2048 key would require magic states with errors around one in 10 billion, roughly a million times cleaner than what Google just achieved.

Google says the next step is running cultivation at a larger scale. The team projects that halving Willow's underlying hardware noise would push magic state errors down to about two in 100,000, because errors in the process shrink with the cube of the chip's noise level.

Two firms control corporate Bitcoin buys, even as business adoption broadens

Bitcoin ownership is broadening, while Strategy and Strive dominate reported accumulation and financing choices shape the flow of fresh corporate buying.

By Liam 'Akiba' Wright Editor-in-Chief • CryptoSlate

01 River’s Oct. 5 snapshot puts Strategy and Strive’s holdings additions above net business growth, showing concentrated accumulation. 02 Strive bought 2,822 BTC during Oct. 12-13, while separately reporting $369.2 million in expected gross warrant proceeds. 03 Strategy spent $192.4 million on STRC buybacks and $21.5 million on Bitcoin during Oct. 5-11, highlighting competing capital uses. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Bitcoin treasury company Strive bought 2,822 BTC during Oct. 12-13, according to a filing released Oct. 14. The purchase adds fresh demand from one of the two firms dominating this year’s reported corporate accumulation.

The update follows River’s Oct. 8 business-adoption report , which put Strategy and Strive’s combined 2026 holdings additions at 197,000 BTC. That exceeded the 193,000 BTC net increase River reported for businesses overall in charts dated Oct. 5.

Strive’s new purchase accompanies a separate financing disclosure. Meanwhile, Strategy reported buying Bitcoin while spending more on repurchasing preferred shares. Both cases show why an expanding roster of corporate holders does not automatically create an equally broad source of new buying.

River’s category chart shows conventional businesses adding about 20,000 BTC and other Bitcoin treasury companies adding about 8,000 BTC in 2026 through Oct. 5, with River’s text reporting 32,800 BTC sold by large miners.

The roughly 4,000 BTC separating those figures cannot be read as a direct measure of market selling by everyone else. Positive additions in some categories coexist with reductions in another, and the displayed totals are rounded.

River also reports a 10% increase over the past year in the number of public companies holding Bitcoin.

For demand to diversify, purchases outside the leading treasury firms would need to carry more weight. A growing holder count measures the spread of ownership; repeated purchases by a wider group would demonstrate a broader source of demand.

Purchases compete with other uses of capital

Strive’s Oct. 14 filing records that the company bought 2,822 BTC during Oct. 12-13 at an average price of approximately $83,266 per coin, including fees and expenses.

For the same two days, it separately reported warrant exercises expected to generate $369.2 million in gross proceeds. It said no traditional warrants issued in its private investment in public equity transaction remained outstanding at the Oct. 13 close.

Those statements do not show that all expected proceeds settled as cash, how much remained after costs, or that those proceeds funded the concurrent purchase.

The absence of remaining traditional PIPE warrants changes that particular financing channel without establishing the size or funding of Strive’s next purchase. The financing disclosure describes a source of capital, subject to the limits of expected gross proceeds.

That latest purchase follows a separate window covered by Strive’s Oct. 13 disclosure . That earlier update reported buying 3,311 BTC during Oct. 5-9 and holding 32,773 BTC as of Oct. 9. It also recorded $310.3 million in cash and equivalents on that date, alongside increases in reported common and preferred share counts.

Related Reading Strive bought $280 million in Bitcoin, but Bitcoin per common share rose just 1.72%

Strategy’s Oct. 12 capital update makes the funding link explicit for its Bitcoin purchases. During Oct. 5-11, it bought 250 BTC for $21.5 million, bringing holdings to 848,250 BTC on Oct. 11.

Of that purchase amount, $21 million came from net proceeds of MSTR common-share sales and $500,000 from dollars. In the same reporting period, Strategy spent $192.4 million repurchasing 1,932,145 STRC preferred shares.

The repurchases were not Bitcoin purchases, and the release did not identify their specific funding source, so the figures do not establish that Strategy sold Bitcoin to pay for the buybacks, or that every dollar spent on STRC otherwise would have bought Bitcoin.

Buying back preferred stock returns funds to the holders of those securities, while acquiring Bitcoin adds coins to the treasury. Both can occur in the same week without implying the same demand in the Bitcoin market.

As of Oct. 11, Strategy held $4.88 billion in its USD Reserve intended to support preferred dividends and debt interest, alongside $640.5 million of cash for broader treasury uses.

Merger transfers complicate the demand measure

Strive’s acquisition of Semler Scientific earlier in 2026 illustrates the difference between growth in one issuer’s holdings and fresh buying across the business sector.

The companies’ Jan. 13 shareholder-approval announcement identified 5,048.1 BTC already held by Semler as part of the all-stock transaction. It also reported Strive’s purchase of 123 BTC, which brought Strive’s holdings to 7,749.8 BTC before the acquisition.

The Jan. 16 closing announcement confirmed that the acquisition had completed and put combined holdings at approximately 12,797.9 BTC. The acquired Semler coins enlarged Strive’s consolidated treasury, but their transfer did not represent another purchase of those coins from the market.

River’s published report and category chart do not explain how its Strategy-and-Strive figure treats the Semler transaction. That leaves no basis for mechanically deducting 5,048.1 BTC from either reported total, or for presenting a precise, merger-adjusted percentage of fresh buying.

An exact share of fresh buying requires separating purchases and sales from coins transferred between corporate owners. River’s figures establish reported holdings concentration while leaving that transaction-level calculation unresolved.

Strive and Strategy bought 3,072 BTC, while transferred coins, share buybacks, and prospective financing added no fresh Bitcoin demand. The two firms’ recent disclosures cover different purchase windows, both extending beyond River’s Oct. 5 snapshot. Adding them to that snapshot would require a new, consistently dated sector account.

For subsequent demand, the useful signals are completed purchases, financing that becomes available cash, and management’s allocation of that cash. Evidence of larger purchases across other businesses would strengthen the case for a broader corporate bid.

Until then, a growing roster of Bitcoin owners and a diversified source of fresh buying remain different propositions.

posts.title: Bitcoin Could Jump 50% If Developers Agree on Quantum Plan: Capriole CEO
posts.titleVi: Bitcoin Could Jump 50% If Developers Agree on Quantum Plan: Capriole CEO
posts.summary: According to Charles Edwards, CEO of Capriole Investments, Bitcoin’s price could rise 30% to 50% in a day if developers agree on a roadmap to protect the blockchain against quantum computers.
posts.summaryVi: According to Charles Edwards, CEO of Capriole Investments, Bitcoin’s price could rise 30% to 50% in a day if developers agree on a roadmap to protect the blockchain against quantum computers.
posts.content:
According to Charles Edwards, CEO of Capriole Investments, Bitcoin’s price could rise 30% to 50% in a day if developers agree on a roadmap to protect the blockchain against quantum computers.

He also warned that delays in addressing the threat could weigh on the asset’s valuation.

Speaking to BMTV, Edwards described the quantum threat as tangible within a typical two- to three-year investment horizon. Bitcoin developers have yet to reach a consensus on a path forward, he noted, despite early-stage proposals intended to help prepare the network.

“If they kind of align and say, okay, this is the roadmap that we’re going to do, or this is the signature schemes that we’re going to probably implement in the next sort of 12 months or 18 months or what have you,” Edwards said, “I think that results in a significant repricing of Bitcoin up.”

He estimated that a concrete plan from Bitcoin Core developers could produce a 30% to 50% price move in one day as investors reassess the threat. The next six to 12 months could therefore be positive for BTC if development progresses. Failure to make headway would leave the network increasingly exposed as technology advances, prompting Edwards to reconsider Bitcoin’s fair value.

Coinbase has also outlined requirements for post-quantum security, arguing that any new signature design must account for transaction fees and the cost of validating transactions across the network. Its October 13 blog discussed possible technical approaches, including hybrid signatures during a transition.

BTC was trading around $81,000 at the time of writing, down nearly 3% in the last 24 hours, with a daily range of $80,400 to $84,000. In the past week, it lost over 2%, although it is up more than 4% from a month ago, while sitting roughly 36% below its all-time high.

According to Edwards, interest rates are a short-term liquidity headwind, though the CEO doubts they will stay high for long because the inflation behind them comes mostly from oil prices tied to the US-Iran conflict.

Mining data provides another reason for cautious optimism. Bitcoin’s hash rate, a measure of computing power committed to secure the network, began recovering four to six weeks ago after a prolonged decline. Edwards views that recovery as evidence that the cycle bottom may be in, although miners shifting capacity toward AI makes future hash rate trends harder to interpret.

He also warned that AI could accelerate quantum development, even though he considers current fears about AI independently breaking Bitcoin’s encryption premature.

Wayne is a dynamic part-time trader with an impressive eye for detail. His passion for understanding financial systems has led to an intriguing interest in blockchain technology, and he enjoys exploring and writing about cryptocurrencies. Possessing a keen intellect and diligent work ethic, he stays up-to-date on the latest industry trends, regularly sharing his insights in articles and professional presentations.

Binance.US seeks $1B valuation in potential $100M funding round: Report

Latest News Published Oct 15, 2026 The crypto exchange was reportedly looking to use the additional funding to regain market share following Binance’s 2023 settlement with US authorities.

Binance.US is reportedly seeking to raise up to $100 million in a funding round that could value the cryptocurrency exchange at $1 billion.

According to a Thursday Bloomberg report , the US-based crypto exchange is pursuing private investment as it looks to expand its business. The potential $1 billion valuation would be well below the $4.5 billion pre-money valuation it secured in 2022, when it raised $200 million in seed funding.

Binance.US reportedly informed World Liberty Financial, the crypto platform co-founded by US President Donald Trump and his sons, about the funding round, but the company will not be participating. Last year, Binance was embroiled in a controversial $2 billion investment between an entity tied to the United Arab Emirates royalty and World Liberty using the platform’s USD1 stablecoin.

The proposed funding round is reportedly part of Binance.US’ efforts to regain market share against larger rivals following a 2023 settlement between Binance Holdings Ltd. and US authorities. As part of the agreement, Binance Holdings agreed to pay $4.3 billion in penalties and accept additional monitoring and oversight, while its then-CEO, Changpeng Zhao, pleaded guilty to a felony charge. Zhao served four months in prison before receiving a pardon from Trump in 2025.

Latest News Published Oct 15, 2026 The crypto exchange was reportedly looking to use the additional funding to regain market share following Binance’s 2023 settlement with US authorities.

Binance.US is reportedly seeking to raise up to $100 million in a funding round that could value the cryptocurrency exchange at $1 billion.

According to a Thursday Bloomberg report , the US-based crypto exchange is pursuing private investment as it looks to expand its business. The potential $1 billion valuation would be well below the $4.5 billion pre-money valuation it secured in 2022, when it raised $200 million in seed funding.

Binance.US reportedly informed World Liberty Financial, the crypto platform co-founded by US President Donald Trump and his sons, about the funding round, but the company will not be participating. Last year, Binance was embroiled in a controversial $2 billion investment between an entity tied to the United Arab Emirates royalty and World Liberty using the platform’s USD1 stablecoin.

The proposed funding round is reportedly part of Binance.US’ efforts to regain market share against larger rivals following a 2023 settlement between Binance Holdings Ltd. and US authorities. As part of the agreement, Binance Holdings agreed to pay $4.3 billion in penalties and accept additional monitoring and oversight, while its then-CEO, Changpeng Zhao, pleaded guilty to a felony charge. Zhao served four months in prison before receiving a pardon from Trump in 2025.

84 million XRP added to exchange wallets as price slipped toward $1.30

The same 699 tracked wallets added 83.94 million XRP across the October 12–15 snapshot window, an increase of about 0.38%.

By Liam 'Akiba' Wright Editor-in-Chief • CryptoSlate

01 The same 699 tracked wallets added 83.94 million XRP across daily changes dated October 13–15, with no new wallets. 02 Binance-attributed wallets added 54.61 million XRP over October 8–15, leading the separate 0.37% weekly increase. 03 The next test is whether the custody build persists alongside seller-initiated spot trading. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Wallets publicly attributed to exchanges added 83.94 million XRP across three daily balance changes dated Oct. 13–15, taking the tracked total to 22.06 billion XRP. The 0.38% increase creates a potential-supply question during price weakness.

XRP Insights, a tracker of XRP Ledger balances and public wallet labels, recorded the rise in the same 699 wallets across 24 exchanges. Its latest exchange-wallet snapshot was taken at 08:01 UTC on Oct. 15, 2026.

XRP traded near $1.32 in a CryptoSlate reading at about 14:56 UTC on Oct. 15. The page showed a 0.89% rise over 24 hours and about $3.12 billion in reported turnover. CryptoSlate also lists broader token prices in its market table .

A three-day build and a separate weekly view

The downloadable balance figures show three successive positive daily changes:

Daily change dated Increase, million XRP Oct. 13, 2026 17.75 Oct. 14, 2026 35.21 Oct. 15, 2026 30.98 Three-change total 83.94 The dates label changes from the preceding day's snapshot. Together, they cover approximately 08:00 UTC on Oct. 12 through 08:01 UTC on Oct. 15. Over that interval, tracked holdings rose from about 21.973 billion to 22.057 billion XRP.

Each observation from Oct. 12 through Oct. 15 retained 699 wallets and 24 exchanges, with no newly added wallets or exchanges excluded for coverage changes.

That consistency matters because discovering another exchange wallet can increase a provider's reported total without any XRP moving. Here, the provider's records show a balance increase within the tracked set.

Related Reading Why XRP’s 63 billion circulating tokens don’t tell buyers what’s for sale

The venue breakdown answers a different question. For Oct. 8–15, XRP Insights reported an increase of 82.35 million XRP, or 0.37%, in the same tracked wallets. That seven-day figure overlaps the latest three daily gains; the two totals cannot be added.

Binance-attributed wallets accounted for 54.61 million XRP of the weekly net increase, the largest positive venue change and roughly two-thirds of the total. Upbit added 11.58 million XRP, Kraken 9.17 million, Coinbase 8.09 million and Bithumb 5.81 million over the same week.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

The build was not uniform. Bybit's tracked holdings fell by 4.22 million XRP, while SBI VC Trade and Bitfinex each declined by about 3.4 million and Uphold by 3.04 million. These offsets help explain why the sum of the largest gains exceeds the net increase.

The venue breakdown covers Oct. 8–15. Binance's 54.61 million XRP addition belongs to that weekly window; the three-day total is an aggregate across the tracked wallets.

Related Reading XRP rebounded as Binance spot turnover fell nearly 80%

XRP Insights counts hot wallets, deposit hubs and cold storage. Exchange-controlled wallets can pool customer balances and institutional custody assets, so the total does not measure XRP available on an order book.

The latest dataset includes about 480.2 million XRP classified as wrapped-token reserves or other funds, including insurance and charity holdings. Binance's grouping also includes Binance-Peg XRP backing and a separately identified Binance.US affiliate wallet.

Shared-address accounting adds another limit. Official XRP Ledger payment documentation explains that destination tags tell an exchange which customer to credit in its own systems. A ledger balance therefore cannot reveal each customer's orders or trading intentions.

The tracker uses validated ledger balances and XRPSCAN wallet labels, carrying forward the last value if a read fails. Transfers between tracked and untracked exchange addresses can alter the measured total without a customer deciding to trade.

Related Reading XRP ETFs now hold $1.7 billion but took in just $4M last week

CryptoSlate's Oct. 8 supply analysis examined the distinction between custody and executable supply. Its Oct. 12 trading report covered Oct. 8–10 spot turnover and earlier futures rebuilding.

Executed trades would test the supply risk

For XRP holders, the immediate question is whether the additional balances accompany sustained selling on the venues involved. Further same-wallet growth alongside seller-initiated spot executions would strengthen that concern. A balance reversal or an identified custody transfer would weaken it.

The next test is seller-initiated spot trading on the same venues and over a defined window: incoming sellers accepting resting buyers' orders.

Direction labels also vary. Coinbase's trade-record definitions define side as the resting order's side: a buy record describes a buyer whose order was met by an incoming seller. Venue-specific definitions therefore matter when measuring seller-initiated activity.

The reported $3.1 billion of 24-hour turnover cannot answer that question. It measures aggregate activity, rather than seller aggression tied to the wallet window.

Written by Sam Bourgi staff editor Edited by Bryan O'Shea staff editor Written by Sam Bourgi staff editor Edited by Bryan O'Shea staff editor

Latest News Published Oct 15, 2026 Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

Today in crypto, a Wall Street Journal investigation revealed that former Trump crypto adviser Bo Hines retained a financial stake in a firm that benefited from a Tether deal while he helped advance US stablecoin legislation. Meanwhile, Ledger introduced an $849 hardware wallet with stronger anti-tampering protections following a security incident in Asia, and Australia’s securities regulator proposed new capital, custody and trading requirements for crypto platforms ahead of a 2027 rollout.

Former White House crypto adviser Bo Hines retained a one-third stake in an investment firm that received millions of dollars from Tether while he was helping advance landmark US stablecoin legislation, according to a Wall Street Journal investigation .

The report found that Nxum, an investment company Hines co-founded, received $6.3 million through an agreement with Tether, with the first payment arriving while Hines was still serving in the Trump administration.

Hines reportedly remained in contact with Nxum partners through Signal, sharing updates on the GENIUS Act and encouraging them to criticize Republican lawmakers who opposed the legislation.

The GENIUS Act , which established a federal regulatory framework for payment stablecoins, was signed into law in July 2025. Hines left the administration shortly afterward, joining Tether as a strategic adviser in August before becoming CEO of its US operations.

The revelations add to scrutiny of financial ties between Trump administration officials and the cryptocurrency industry. Several former regulators have also moved into senior industry positions, including former CFTC Commissioner Summer Mersinger, who became CEO of the Blockchain Association.

Ledger unveiled a new device on Thursday with stronger protections against tampering , days after confirming that wallets sold through a reseller in Asia contained malicious implants.

The French hardware wallet maker introduced Atom, an $849 device that combines a crypto wallet with everyday apps through a smartphone-like design. Atom separates Android apps from sensitive wallet operations and includes protections Ledger says would block the implants used in the recent Asia incident. It’s also advertised to detect tampering even when switched off.

The company expects to begin shipping the device in summer 2027, according to an announcement shared with Cointelegraph.

Ledger said Atom will also support AI agent approvals, encrypted messaging and post-quantum cryptography.

The announcement follows a security incident that surfaced on Friday involving malicious implants found in wallets sold through authorized reseller CryptoBilis. Ledger has requested that distributors in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong suspend sales of its products. European retail chain MediaMarkt has also pulled Ledger wallets off its shelves .

Australia’s securities regulator opened consultation Thursday on proposed capital, custody and trading requirements for crypto platforms, as it prepares to implement legislation passed in April that expands oversight of the industry.

The proposals include three alternative capital models, restrictions on platforms trading for their own account and quarterly reporting of wallets holding customer assets. ASIC also proposes allowing offshore custody while seeking feedback on safeguards if an overseas parent or related company fails.

“Our proposed guidance and standards acknowledge the increasing role of digital assets and tokenization, including in traditional parts of the financial system,” said ASIC Commissioner Alan Kirkland.

The proposed guidance and standards would give crypto operators greater clarity on requirements to obtain a license, safeguard customer assets and meet financial requirements under the new framework. The consultation follows Parliament’s passage of the Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act earlier this year.

posts.summaryVi: Hotter-than-expected US inflation data, along with the KOSPI index’s crash in South Korea, weighed heavily on the cryptocurrency market. Bitcoin (BTC) slipped below $80,000, while most altcoins followed suit, posting steeper declines.
posts.content:
Hotter-than-expected US inflation data, along with the KOSPI index’s crash in South Korea, weighed heavily on the cryptocurrency market. Bitcoin (BTC) slipped below $80,000, while most altcoins followed suit, posting steeper declines.

Pi Network’s PI couldn’t escape the broader correction, plunging to around $0.077, or its lowest level since July. Many investors have likely grown weary of the token’s major downfall over the past several months, so we asked three of the most popular AI-powered chatbots for their outlook on the remainder of the year. Here’s what they had to say.

ChatGPT leaned bearish, expecting the price to sustain its current level or even plunge to a new all-time low of around $0.06 sometime in Q4. OpenAI’s platform claimed that the constant PI token unlocks are the main factor preventing a decisive comeback. It also cited KYC issues reported by some Pioneers and migration struggles as additional hurdles.

On the other hand, ChatGPT sees potential for a significant rebound in the coming months, but only if protocol 28 deploys successfully and prices sustain a recovery above $0.10. While the upgrade is scheduled for tomorrow (October 16), it won’t be a surprise if it gets delayed, since the Core Team has a habit of postponing important developments.

Perplexity also warned of an additional downside risk that could drive the price down to $0.05. The chatbot estimated that such a collapse has a 15% to 25% probability of happening sometime during the final quarter of 2026, while the base case for PI is to trade between $0.07 and $0.10.

Google’s Gemini seemed more favorable to a price increase, suggesting that a rise to $0.15 is mathematically and technically possible. It added an important disclaimer that such a pump would depend on several catalysts, including the protocol 28 upgrade, further ecosystem developments, and listings on major exchanges.

“A surprise spot listing on Binance or Coinbase during Q4 would unlock significant retail and institutional buying liquidity, typically sparking short-term price surges capable of pushing a micro-cap asset past key resistance barriers ($0.10, $0.12, and up to $0.15),” it explained.

X user Crypto With Gopal is among the few to address PI lately, and his analysis points to a cautious approach. He assumed that a breakout above $0.10-$0.105 could open the door toward $0.15, but that represents a solid 42% increase from current levels.

“Until then, $0.075-$0.08 is a key support zone to watch; losing it could signal further downside. Sentiment: cautiously watching for reversal. A confirmed neckline is needed to validate the double-bottom setup,” he concluded.

Dimitar got interested in cryptocurrencies back in 2018 amid the prolonged bear market. His biggest passion in the field is Bitcoin and he was fascinated with its journey. With a flair for producing high-quality content, he started covering the cryptocurrency space in late 2018. His hobby is football.

Decrypt News Business Boom or Bust, Bitcoin Wins the AI Trade, Bitwise CIO Says

In a note to investors, Matt Hougan used a “Choose Your Own Adventure” framework to argue that superabundance, an AI bust or a muddle-through economy all ultimately funnel to the same place: Bitcoin higher.

By Decrypt Staff Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan argued in an investor note that Bitcoin benefits across nearly every macro scenario, framing it like the “Choose Your Own Adventure” books where different paths reach the same ending.

If AI delivers “superabundance,” value flows to scarce assets like Bitcoin; if the AI bubble bursts, he sees a near-certain government bailout and money-printing that Bitcoin “was built for.”

He hedged—citing Bitcoin’s 50% COVID drop and risks like a crackdown or quantum computing, but concluded macro “matters less than most people think.”

No matter how the AI story ends, Bitwise’s chief investment officer argues, the trade leads to the same place: Bitcoin higher.

In a note to investors published Wednesday, Matt Hougan laid out his case using the “Choose Your Own Adventure” books of his childhood, where wildly different choices often funneled readers to the same ending.

He said the range of macro outcomes facing investors today is the widest he’s seen in his career, with pundits split between AI doubling GDP and AI causing human extinction. His answer was to walk down each path and see where it leads.

If AI delivers “superabundance,” Hougan wrote, productivity explodes and intelligence-based work gets cheap, but that abundance becomes a tailwind for genuinely scarce assets, as value migrates to things that can’t be reproduced, like waterfront land, gold, and Bitcoin.

If the AI bubble bursts instead, triggering a 2008-style recession, Bitcoin initially sells off with other risk assets, but Hougan argued a government bailout would follow, and given that the AI buildout is “the biggest infrastructure investment in the history of America,” the resulting money-printing would be enormous.

“This is exactly the environment bitcoin was built for,” he wrote, putting the odds of a bailout at “nearly 100%.”

The third path, a muddle-through of roughly 3% growth and 4% rates, simply lets Bitcoin keep doing what it’s been doing: drawing ETF flows, advisor adoption and corporate and sovereign balance-sheet allocations as government debt mounts. “Bitcoin wins by showing up,” he wrote.

The memo lands amid exactly the kind of macro anxiety Hougan is addressing. BlackRock CEO Larry Fink warned this week that a halt to data center construction could tip the U.S. into recession, underscoring how tightly AI infrastructure and the broader economy have become intertwined.

Hougan was careful to hedge. He stressed Bitcoin won’t rise in a straight line, noting it fell 50% in days during the 2020 COVID panic before rebounding roughly 20-fold, and acknowledged the thesis could break for non-macro reasons. Among them: a global government crackdown or the quantum-computing threat to older wallets, a rising risk even as researchers debate whether AI could break crypto’s encryption before quantum computers arrive.

Still, his conclusion was unequivocal: for long-term investors, the big macro questions “matter less than most people think,” because nearly every path still ends with Bitcoin.

News South Korea Image by CryptoSlate Hacks

South Korea names two crypto firms in breach wave that also hit major banks

Streami and Pravang are among 16 affected financial companies as the FSC outlines plans for a wider security overhaul.

By Liam 'Akiba' Wright Editor-in-Chief • CryptoSlate

01 The FSC named Streami and Pravang among 16 financial companies affected by recent customer-data breaches. 02 About 100,000 customer-data items were exposed across affected firms, and the FSC provided no company-level breakdown. 03 The FSC plans wider inspections, faster threat sharing and more frequent testing, beginning with larger financial companies. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

South Korea's Financial Services Commission has named crypto businesses Streami and Pravang among 16 financial companies hit by recent data breaches, alongside major banks.

The FSC's October 14 disclosure lists the two virtual asset businesses alongside Shinhan, Kookmin, Busan and Hana banks and companies in other financial sectors. Streami operates the Gopax exchange ; Pravang is the other crypto business named in the release.

The FSC estimated the exposure at about 100,000 pieces of customer data across the affected companies, including names, contact details, resident registration numbers and email addresses. The FSC did not publish a company-level breakdown.

As of the October 14 meeting, authorities had not identified leaked account passwords or credit card numbers, according to the FSC's English release .

Related Reading Revolut tricked into handing hackers the passports and Bitcoin histories of wealthy customers

The Financial Supervisory Service and Financial Security Institute are investigating the attack methods, whether the incidents are linked, whether a common attacker was responsible and whether AI was used. The number of affected firms could also rise as companies check their systems against attacker IP addresses shared by authorities.

A wider security check found weaknesses beyond the confirmed breach list. All 555 companies completed a 12-point checklist by October 8, with 425 reporting their arrangements were appropriate and 130 reporting areas needing improvement. The checklist was a sector-wide self-assessment.

The shortcomings were mainly in security patches and monitoring systems. Reported gaps included missing software updates, weak management of systems no longer supported by their vendors, absent round-the-clock monitoring and weaknesses in authentication or access controls. Companies submitted remedial plans and had begun taking corrective steps.

FSC plans broader checks and clearer accountability

The proposed response reaches across financial companies' security management, from their connections to outside systems to the executives responsible for overseeing controls. The FSC plans a comprehensive review of external connections, authentication and access controls, with clearer reporting lines and responsibilities for chief executives, chief information security officers and chief information officers.

One proposal would require vulnerability assessments at least twice a year, starting with large financial companies. The existing general requirement for financial companies and electronic financial businesses is annual testing, while external websites already have to be checked twice yearly.

Regulators also plan faster sharing of threat information detected by companies, AI threat-level information and AI-based infrastructure for finding vulnerabilities. The package includes plans for more security support for smaller firms, alongside stronger CEO accountability and more effective sanctions.

The FSC also intends to accelerate consideration of easing rules on separating computer networks to enable AI-based defenses.

The inspection's detailed scope and schedule had yet to be agreed. The release did not specify whether each proposed financial-company measure would cover virtual asset businesses.

News Analysis At the White House, crypto policy vacancy looms large

The departure of President Donald Trump's crypto adviser, Patrick Witt, leaves the digital assets office vacant and its policy aims uncertain.

By Jesse Hamilton | Edited by Nikhilesh De Oct 15, 2026, 2:48 p.m. EDT

4 min read Make preferred on Share 

Patrick Witt's exit leaves President Donald Trump's White House without a named crypto adviser. (Jesse Hamilton/CoinDesk) Summary Show The exit of President Donald Trump’s crypto adviser, Patrick Witt, wasn’t a surprise, but it leaves the White House without an explicit digital assets policy presence. The White House insists that crypto is still a priority, but its recent naming of a new AI czar left crypto off the role despite its previous inclusion.

When President Donald Trump returned to the White House last year, he not only shed his earlier resistance to crypto technology but embraced the industry with the hiring of a high-profile crypto czar and the establishment of his President’s Council of Advisors for Digital Assets.

Almost two years later, that policy push seems to have gone quiet for the moment, with the departure of Patrick Witt, who had been the final crypto adviser running that office. And when the president recently ushered in a new artificial intelligence czar, the job that was once split between crypto and AI seemed to have dropped its crypto remit.

So who is minding the store for crypto policy at the White House? It's not clear, even as a handful of people on Capitol Hill continue to suggest that the final weeks of the congressional session after the November elections could still see some legislative action for the industry. The White House still has a staff of policy advisers, and Trump's administration now boasts several crypto regulatory irons in the fire at agencies such as the Securities and Exchange Commission. But no new name has been explicitly attached to Trump's in-house crypto initiatives.

A White House official told CoinDesk on Thursday that Witt's work was appreciated and wished him "the best of luck in the future endeavors." The official didn’t comment on who would be taking over.

"Crypto and Clarity Act will continue to be a priority for the president," the official said.

The White House's digital assets policy work was never a large operation, but the advisers were highly vocal at times, and their presence could put an important administrative stamp on crypto goals. The effort began several weeks before Trump returned to office in 2025, when the president-elect named David Sacks , the former PayPal executive, as his incoming AI and crypto czar.

Trump also tapped a little-known former college football player, Bo Hines, to be the first director of the digital assets advisory council — at first a one-person effort, but eventually adding a deputy. Hines quickly became the crypto face of the White House, taking constant meetings with crypto insiders and appearing on event stages. And his brief tenure of about eight months concluded with a major win for the industry in Congress: the passage of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act into law.

A White House signing and celebration ensued, in which many of the most prominent names in crypto enjoyed front-row seats. Less than two weeks later, the administration released a comprehensive crypto agenda that set out its specific plans for fostering the sector in the U.S.

Having helped establish the U.S. law for stablecoin issuers, Hines took a job running the U.S. arm of the leading issuer, Tether. Meanwhile, a consulting firm he set up with his father and another partner, Nxum, was also paid millions of dollars as the main provider of services for a new political action committee , first revealed in reporting by CoinDesk. The super PAC was funded mostly by Tether's U.S. financial partner, Cantor Fitzgerald, and led by a Tether exec.

This week, the Wall Street Journal reported that Hines' Nxum, had received payments from Tether for consulting services while Hines was at the White House working on the GENIUS Act.

Hines' deputy on the council, Witt, took over for Hines as its new executive director. Another former football star, Witt also had a greater depth of Washington experience, and he became the face of the White House's push for the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act. Over the ensuing months of negotiations, Witt didn't conceal his frustration, regularly taking to social media site X to fume about those he saw as getting in the way of the Senate bill that would erect a U.S. regulatory scaffold for crypto markets.

During that legislative process, Sacks stepped down from the czar role in March, leaving Witt and his deputy, Harry Jung, trying to manage the administration's crypto stance. That was complicated by the fact that President Trump's own crypto empire figured prominently in the talks, as Democrats demanded that senior government officials be blocked from personal crypto ties.

As the negotiations dragged further into the year — and closer to the elections — the White House offered some concessions that would have applied unprecedented ethics constraints on the president's digital assets involvement, though Democrats concluded that the agreement didn't go far enough.

Witt had confirmed in July that he had military-service commitments on the horizon with the Georgia National Guard, but he stayed to complete Clarity Act negotiations, even as his deputy left to join Hines’ Nxum. The legislation slammed into a political roadblock a month ago, failing to advance in a Senate floor vote before the chamber dispersed for a lengthy break leading up to next month's elections.

Following rumors this week that Witt had already exited, he posted Wednesday night at around midnight to confirm his departure. He thanked agency chiefs and lawmakers that had helped with Clarity, saying that "with regulators and elected officials like you, I rest easy knowing the future of digital asset innovation in America is bright." He said he'd be moving into the private sector.

Crypto insiders say they aren't sure who they'll be dealing with as their market-structure hopes have largely fizzled for the moment.

When Trump moved earlier this month to re-establish an AI overseer , hiring former SEC Chairman and current intelligence director Jay Clayton to lead his Super Intelligence Force, the job no longer mentions a crypto element. While AI and crypto enjoy some overlapping territory, Clayton comes with a rocky crypto history, having been the SEC chief that first began its stance that would be labeled "regulation by enforcement."

Speaking after BlackRock’s Q3 earnings, Fink said AI infrastructure spending has become so central to growth that a construction halt would be dangerous—calling the backlash “misinformation” as data centers become a midterm flashpoint.

By Decrypt Staff Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

BlackRock CEO Larry Fink. Image: Shutterstock/Decrypt

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

BlackRock CEO Larry Fink says a U.S. moratorium on data center construction would trigger a recession, saying “so much of our economy is based on the build-out of this capex.”

He dismissed the mounting backlash—over electricity, water and grid strain—as “misinformation,” insisting “data centers are not the problem."

The warning matters for crypto given Bitcoin’s macro sensitivity.

BlackRock CEO Larry Fink has a blunt warning about what could derail the U.S. economy: slamming the brakes on the data centers powering the AI boom.

Speaking to CNBC on Wednesday after BlackRock posted better-than-expected third-quarter earnings, Fink said the surge in AI infrastructure spending has become so central to economic growth that choking it off would be dangerous.

“If we have a moratorium of some sort in this country, we will be in a recession,” he said, adding that “so much of our economy is based on the build-out of this capex.”

The comments come as data centers have become a flashpoint ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections, with local opposition mounting over their electricity demands, water use and strain on power grids.

According to Brookings, at least 100 localities had approved moratoriums by July, and New York has paused certain permits for up to a year. Fink pushed back on the backlash, calling much of it “misinformation” and insisting that “data centers are not the problem,” pointing instead to the construction jobs and energy-infrastructure demand the buildout is generating.

The scale of the spending underscores his argument. Wall Street analysts estimate AI capital expenditures could top $1 trillion in 2027 and exceed $5 trillion cumulatively through 2030, making the sector a meaningful driver of the roughly 3% annualized GDP growth Fink wants to sustain. He has argued more private capital is needed to keep it going, and said BlackRock has spoken with chipmakers including AMD and Broadcom about the effort.

But Fink is swimming against a sharply rising tide of public opposition . An Annenberg Public Policy Center survey this summer found 61% of Americans oppose new data centers in their area, up from 49% in the spring, with majorities of Democrats, Republicans and independents all against them.

The concerns center on soaring electricity demand, water use and strain on local grids. That backlash has already produced real restrictions : New York has a moratorium on hyperscale data centers, Texas has paused approvals, and cities from Austin to Jersey City have imposed limits , with Data Center Watch counting roughly $130 billion in projects blocked or delayed in the first quarter of 2026 alone.

It has also become a live electoral issue. The fight is central to Ohio’s Senate race, where Democrat Sherrod Brown has campaigned against the buildout, and a super PAC backed by AI billionaires including Marc Andreessen and OpenAI President Greg Brockman has poured millions into ads defending data centers across battleground states. President Donald Trump has weighed in too, warning that communities resisting the facilities risk ending up “backwards and poor.”

Against that backdrop, Fink pushed back directly, suggesting the AI buildout in the United States is propping up the U.S. economy and any shift would result in a significant downturn.

The warning carries weight for crypto, given how closely Bitcoin now tracks broader risk sentiment and macro conditions.

Fink, who runs the world’s largest asset manager and oversees its dominant spot Bitcoin ETF, has become one of Wall Street’s most prominent crypto converts . He has called Bitcoin an asset for a “ frightened world ” and framed it as a legitimate alternative investment, while BlackRock has flagged AI agents as a potential next wave of crypto demand .

Against that backdrop, Fink pushed back directly, suggesting the AI buildout in the United States is propping up the U.S. economy and any shift would result in a significant downturn.

The warning carries weight for crypto, given how closely Bitcoin now tracks broader risk sentiment and macro conditions.

Fink, who runs the world’s largest asset manager and oversees its dominant spot Bitcoin ETF, has become one of Wall Street’s most prominent crypto converts . He has called Bitcoin an asset for a “ frightened world ” and framed it as a legitimate alternative investment, while BlackRock has flagged AI agents as a potential next wave of crypto demand .

Machi loses $269,000 on ETH, then opens another long seven minutes later

Hyperliquid force-liquidated 1,650 ETH early on Oct. 15, and the tracked wallet held a new 2,500 ETH long by 13:16 BST.

By Liam 'Akiba' Wright Editor-in-Chief • CryptoSlate

01 Machi's tracked wallet had 1,650 ETH force-liquidated across 232 fills, recording about $269,225 in losses before fees. 02 The first new long began 6 minutes 55 seconds after the last forced fill, initially building to 320 ETH. 03 By 13:16 BST, the wallet had rebuilt a 2,500 ETH long at an average entry near $2,370.34. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

A Hyperliquid wallet tracked by Lookonchain as belonging to Machi had 1,650 ETH force-liquidated on the derivatives exchange Hyperliquid early on Oct. 15, then began reopening a long about seven minutes after the last forced fill. By 1:16 p.m. BST, the tracked wallet held a new 2,500 ETH position, again betting on higher prices.

Hyperliquid's public data for the wallet records 232 liquidation fills between 3:22:25 a.m. and 3:24:32 a.m. BST. They executed between $2,330.30 and $2,380.30 and recorded approximately $269,225 in realized trading losses, excluding about $1,087 in fill fees.

The liquidation followed substantial voluntary selling. From 2 p.m. BST on Oct. 14 through the last forced fill the following morning, the wallet voluntarily closed another 4,000 ETH, recording approximately $302,312 in realized losses before fees.

The two loss figures cover separate trade categories: 250 ETH of the voluntary closes occurred during the forced-close window.

Buying resumed at 3:31:27 a.m. BST. By 3:56 a.m., the wallet had accumulated a 320 ETH long at an average entry price of about $2,355.53.

By 1:16 p.m. BST, the wallet had rebuilt a 2,500 ETH long at an average entry price of about $2,370.34.

Related Reading Ethereum open interest rose 2.3% in ETH on Binance as its dollar value fell 6.6%

A separate Hyperliquid transaction shows 250,000 USDC arriving at the tracked address's spot balance at 10:48 a.m. BST.

Hyperliquid's liquidation rules explain how funds can remain after a forced close. Positions become eligible for liquidation when equity falls below maintenance margin. If order-book sales restore the required margin, remaining collateral stays with the trader. A forced closure can therefore leave an account able to trade again.

Decrypt News Artificial Intelligence Google Says AI Isn't Building Itself Yet—Even Though It Writes 75% of the Code

Google DeepMind's first internal audit of AI-driven research finds no measurable speedup in AI progress.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Google DeepMind found no statistically significant acceleration in the pace of its AI progress after April 1, 2026; its capability index has climbed a steady 0.1 points a month.

Most production code at the lab is now more than 75% AI-written, but about 88% of code changes still need humans to steer the AI or write code themselves.

Gemini 4 Argon solved roughly half of the internal research engineering tasks it finished, far below the 90% score DeepMind treats as a red flag for full automation.

Google DeepMind went looking for proof that AI is speeding up the development of AI itself. It didn’t find any.

In the safety report for Gemini 4 Argon, its most powerful model, the lab concluded AI research isn’t moving any faster, even though AI now writes most of the code DeepMind’s engineers ship.

The finding cuts against the scenario that has spooked AI executives into calling for a slowdown. It’s called recursive self-improvement: an AI builds a smarter version of itself, which builds an even smarter one, until progress outruns anyone’s ability to test, regulate, or switch it off—what the report calls “a situation where existing guardrails are severely inadequate.”

“There is currently no significant end-to-end acceleration of ML R&D, AI-driven or otherwise,” Haydn Belfield, a Google DeepMind researcher who worked on the assessment, wrote in a thread on X . “We therefore conclude that the risk from AI-driven ML R&D is currently low.”

ML R&D is shorthand for machine learning research and development, the work of building new AI models.

1/9 In the Gemini 4 Argon Safety & Security Report, we published our first holistic empirical assessment of ML R&D automation and acceleration inside Google DeepMind — combining capability benchmarks, a macro capability index, data on AI-written code and trajectory outcomes, and… pic.twitter.com/Vr8Q5Obbsp

— Haydn Belfield (@HaydnBelfield) October 14, 2026

DeepMind tracks the issue because “AI could speed up frontier capability gains faster than safety, governance, and societal adaptation can keep pace,” Belfield wrote. More automation also means giving AI agents broader access to company systems, more room for a misaligned model (one pursuing goals its makers never intended) to cause trouble.

To measure progress, the team built GCI v1, an internal index that blends the scores of 123 AI models across 92 benchmarks into a single number per model—think of it as an IQ score for AI. “Frontier Gemini capabilities have improved at a remarkably steady pace of ~0.1 GCI points/month,” Belfield wrote.

In the report’s chart of that index, Gemini 1.5 Pro sits near 0.5 points in late 2024 and Gemini 3.8 Flash just above 2.9 in September 2026, with nearly every release hugging a straight line. Argon is the one dot poking above it, at roughly 3.3, though its error bar (the range its true score could plausibly fall in) stretches low enough to touch the trend.

“While Gemini 4 Argon sits above [the] trend, we trace this to increased compute and organizational investment rather than reflecting AI-driven acceleration,” Belfield wrote. Google unveiled Gemini 4 Argon on September 30.

Most production code at DeepMind is now more than 75% AI-written, and the share of fully delegated pull requests (bundles of code changes submitted for review before they go live) rose from 7.5% to 11.9% between April and September. But “~88% of pull requests still require multi-turn human steering or human code authorship—and code changes remain subject to human review before submission,” Belfield wrote.

A survey of 12 senior DeepMind leaders and researchers found automation is highest in “well-specified, verifiable execution tasks and lowest in open-ended scientific ideation, novel experimental design, diagnosing subtle training instabilities, and long-horizon research taste.” In plain terms, AI is great at executing instructions and bad at deciding which ideas are worth chasing.

DeepMind also reviewed 1,389 logs of Argon working as an agent inside the company. The bigger the task, the less likely the model finished it alone and the more often a human stepped in.

The report landed a month after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei argued that recursive self-improvement is already accelerating, a warning Sam Altman and Elon Musk endorsed and one that sent chip stocks down almost 6% . Days earlier, former Anthropic engineer Jacob Coxon had quit the industry , warning AI could “kill us all by the end of the decade.”

DeepMind’s numbers cover only its own lab, and the same report says it can’t rule out that an unrestricted Argon crosses its danger thresholds for cyberattacks and bioweapons information.

Decrypt News Artificial Intelligence Google Says AI Isn't Building Itself Yet—Even Though It Writes 75% of the Code

Google DeepMind's first internal audit of AI-driven research finds no measurable speedup in AI progress.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Google DeepMind found no statistically significant acceleration in the pace of its AI progress after April 1, 2026; its capability index has climbed a steady 0.1 points a month.

Most production code at the lab is now more than 75% AI-written, but about 88% of code changes still need humans to steer the AI or write code themselves.

Gemini 4 Argon solved roughly half of the internal research engineering tasks it finished, far below the 90% score DeepMind treats as a red flag for full automation.

Google DeepMind went looking for proof that AI is speeding up the development of AI itself. It didn’t find any.

In the safety report for Gemini 4 Argon, its most powerful model, the lab concluded AI research isn’t moving any faster, even though AI now writes most of the code DeepMind’s engineers ship.

The finding cuts against the scenario that has spooked AI executives into calling for a slowdown. It’s called recursive self-improvement: an AI builds a smarter version of itself, which builds an even smarter one, until progress outruns anyone’s ability to test, regulate, or switch it off—what the report calls “a situation where existing guardrails are severely inadequate.”

“There is currently no significant end-to-end acceleration of ML R&D, AI-driven or otherwise,” Haydn Belfield, a Google DeepMind researcher who worked on the assessment, wrote in a thread on X . “We therefore conclude that the risk from AI-driven ML R&D is currently low.”

ML R&D is shorthand for machine learning research and development, the work of building new AI models.

1/9 In the Gemini 4 Argon Safety & Security Report, we published our first holistic empirical assessment of ML R&D automation and acceleration inside Google DeepMind — combining capability benchmarks, a macro capability index, data on AI-written code and trajectory outcomes, and… pic.twitter.com/Vr8Q5Obbsp

— Haydn Belfield (@HaydnBelfield) October 14, 2026

DeepMind tracks the issue because “AI could speed up frontier capability gains faster than safety, governance, and societal adaptation can keep pace,” Belfield wrote. More automation also means giving AI agents broader access to company systems, more room for a misaligned model (one pursuing goals its makers never intended) to cause trouble.

To measure progress, the team built GCI v1, an internal index that blends the scores of 123 AI models across 92 benchmarks into a single number per model—think of it as an IQ score for AI. “Frontier Gemini capabilities have improved at a remarkably steady pace of ~0.1 GCI points/month,” Belfield wrote.

In the report’s chart of that index, Gemini 1.5 Pro sits near 0.5 points in late 2024 and Gemini 3.8 Flash just above 2.9 in September 2026, with nearly every release hugging a straight line. Argon is the one dot poking above it, at roughly 3.3, though its error bar (the range its true score could plausibly fall in) stretches low enough to touch the trend.

“While Gemini 4 Argon sits above [the] trend, we trace this to increased compute and organizational investment rather than reflecting AI-driven acceleration,” Belfield wrote. Google unveiled Gemini 4 Argon on September 30.

Most production code at DeepMind is now more than 75% AI-written, and the share of fully delegated pull requests (bundles of code changes submitted for review before they go live) rose from 7.5% to 11.9% between April and September. But “~88% of pull requests still require multi-turn human steering or human code authorship—and code changes remain subject to human review before submission,” Belfield wrote.

A survey of 12 senior DeepMind leaders and researchers found automation is highest in “well-specified, verifiable execution tasks and lowest in open-ended scientific ideation, novel experimental design, diagnosing subtle training instabilities, and long-horizon research taste.” In plain terms, AI is great at executing instructions and bad at deciding which ideas are worth chasing.

DeepMind also reviewed 1,389 logs of Argon working as an agent inside the company. The bigger the task, the less likely the model finished it alone and the more often a human stepped in.

The report landed a month after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei argued that recursive self-improvement is already accelerating, a warning Sam Altman and Elon Musk endorsed and one that sent chip stocks down almost 6% . Days earlier, former Anthropic engineer Jacob Coxon had quit the industry , warning AI could “kill us all by the end of the decade.”

DeepMind’s numbers cover only its own lab, and the same report says it can’t rule out that an unrestricted Argon crosses its danger thresholds for cyberattacks and bioweapons information.
