posts.title: Starknet Considers Becoming an L1 to Reach Quantum Resistance by 2027
posts.titleVi: Starknet Considers Becoming an L1 to Reach Quantum Resistance by 2027
posts.summary: Starknet is considering becoming a standalone Layer 1 blockchain, with its builders targeting quantum-resistant security by 2027 as concerns grow about whether artificial intelligence could accelerate attacks on existing cryptography.
posts.summaryVi: Starknet is considering becoming a standalone Layer 1 blockchain, with its builders targeting quantum-resistant security by 2027 as concerns grow about whether artificial intelligence could accelerate attacks on existing cryptography.
posts.content:
Starknet is considering becoming a standalone Layer 1 blockchain, with its builders targeting quantum-resistant security by 2027 as concerns grow about whether artificial intelligence could accelerate attacks on existing cryptography.

The move would give the network more control over its security upgrades rather than leaving parts of its migration dependent on Ethereum.

In a post on X, Starknet announced that it was “actively considering becoming an L1,” describing the change as a route toward becoming “the first fully quantum-resistant network,” with 2027 as its target.

Starknet already uses zero-knowledge STARK proofs based on hash-based cryptography and has an active roadmap for post-quantum security. But as a Layer 2 on Ethereum, the network still relies on its parent chain for some of its security.

Two areas are still outside the direct control of its builders, including bridge messaging, which uses elliptic-curve cryptography to communicate between Starknet and Ethereum. If that dependency is removed before an Ethereum upgrade, the bridge could break.

The second concerns data availability. Starknet publishes state data to Ethereum through blobs secured by KZG commitments, which rely on cryptography vulnerable to sufficiently powerful quantum computers. A failure in KZG would affect data availability, although Starknet’s STARK proofs would continue to protect the validity of its state.

Ethereum is targeting full Layer 1 quantum resistance by the end of 2029. Starknet’s proposed 2027 timeline would therefore put it ahead of its parent network, provided it can complete the remaining work and settle the architectural questions involved in becoming an independent chain.

The proposal follows growing concerns about advances in AI-assisted mathematics. On October 7, Ethereum researcher Justin Drake urged the blockchain industry to begin preparing for what he called “bunker mode,” recommending a controlled migration of assets to addresses whose public keys remain hidden. However, Vitalik Buterin warned against rushing the process.

Starknet co-founder Eli Ben-Sasson raised similar concerns in posts on October 8, arguing that AI could bring cryptographic threats closer than expected. He identified cryptographic choice and the ability to upgrade security systems as the two foundations of post-quantum readiness.

Starknet has already developed infrastructure that could help it operate independently, including STRK staking and multiple sequencers. However, it would still need to resolve data availability, final settlement, and changes to its official bridge.

Still, the bridge question carries particular weight, especially considering that today, Ethereum verifies Starknet withdrawal proofs before bridged funds can be released. If Starknet becomes an L1, it could continue posting STARK proofs to Ethereum, preserving a connection between the networks, or sever that dependency entirely. But those approaches would create different security assumptions for users.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Decrypt News Artificial Intelligence Developer Who Cloned Photoshop With AI Just Did the Same to Microsoft Office

Developer Brandon Thomas used Anthropic's Claude to build free, open-source replicas of Word, Excel and PowerPoint. They're rough, but they show how cheap cloning software has become.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Developer Brandon Thomas released WordCraft, GridCraft and DeckCraft, free open-source clones of Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint written in Rust with help from Anthropic's Claude.

WordCraft covers 88% of Word's ribbon features and GridCraft handles 513 of Excel's 523 worksheet functions, but the team rates them only 50% to 60% ready for real work.

The release follows Thomas' ArtCraft clones of Adobe's apps and targets a Microsoft 365 subscription that costs $99.99 a year for a single user.

You have two options: Pay $100 every year for Microsoft Office online, or pay nothing for the vibe-coded “Office” clone that does basically the same and runs fully offline. Which do you pick?

The developer who used AI to rebuild Adobe's Creative Cloud for free has now turned to Microsoft Office, releasing open-source clones of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint built with Anthropic's Claude.

Brandon Thomas, the engineer behind the ArtCraft project, published the apps on GitHub as WordCraft , GridCraft and DeckCraft . Open source means anyone can read, copy, and modify the code, and the MIT and Apache 2.0 licenses let people reuse it even commercially.

Earlier this month, Thomas made noise with ArtCraft, a set of free apps mirroring Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, and Lightroom, built with Claude Opus 5.5 after Adobe charged him its cancellation fee one too many times. It landed in the middle of a wave of AI cloning that has seen a developer get GTA V running natively on an iPhone and modders throw Minecraft creepers at an Elden Ring boss.

The Office clones are written in Rust, a programming language known for speed and for blocking the memory bugs that make software crash. A single codebase runs natively on Windows, macOS, Linux and BSD, and also inside a web browser.

Thomas calls the project a clean-room rebuild, meaning the apps were written from public file-format specifications and by watching how the originals behave, never by copying Microsoft's code. It's the same legal approach Compaq used to clone IBM's PC BIOS, the basic startup software of early PCs, back in the 1980s.

WordCraft reads and writes .docx, Word's native file format, and covers 88% of the features in Word's ribbon, the strip of tabs and buttons along the top of the screen. Track changes, footnotes, citations and mail merge—the tool that pulls names from a spreadsheet to personalize hundreds of letters—are already in.

Counting file fidelity and stability, though, the team estimates WordCraft is only about 60% of the way to replacing Word for real work. It's still labeled alpha, an early test version where bugs come standard.

We tried it. It’s only 91Mb, feels snappy and looks almost the same as the normal Microsoft Word. For everyday office jobs, this can easily replace the premium suite.

GridCraft, the Excel clone, already handles 513 of Excel's 523 worksheet functions, the formulas like SUM or VLOOKUP that make spreadsheets do math, plus 89% of its ribbon commands. Its own developers rate it about 50% ready for real work, with compatibility on real-world .xlsx files next on the to-do list. In other words, it knows almost every formula but may still trip over your company's budget spreadsheet.

DeckCraft, the PowerPoint stand-in, covers about 79% of PowerPoint's features and 93% of the core ones, according to its GitHub page. It opens and saves .pptx files, runs transitions and animations, and exports to PDF, but it hasn't reached its first alpha yet.

Every button in all three apps doubles as a command that an AI agent, a model that takes multi-step actions on its own, can trigger. They plug in through MCP, the Model Context Protocol , a standard Anthropic created so AI models can operate outside tools. In practice, a user could ask Claude to build a chart in a spreadsheet or reformat a report without touching the mouse.

Microsoft charges $99.99 a year for Microsoft 365 Personal and $129.99 for the family plan, which is how most households get Word and Excel today. A free look-alike that opens the same files is a direct shot at that bill.

Free Office alternatives have existed for decades: OpenOffice.org was born when Sun Microsystems released the code of its StarOffice suite in October 2000, and LibreOffice split off from it in 2010. Both took years of work by large developer communities, while Thomas shipped his three apps less than two weeks after the Adobe clones, working with an AI model.

Its design is very similar to the Microsoft Office suite, so heavy users should not struggle too much with the switch, which is the main reason preventing people from switching software providers.

The model behind ArtCraft, Claude Opus 5.5, launched September 22 at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens; tokens are the chunks of text an AI reads and writes, and the unit AI companies bill by.

On Terminal-Bench 4.0, which tests whether an AI agent can finish complex professional tasks in a command-line environment and scores the share of tasks completed, Opus 5.5 hit 66.4%.

Thomas also has a habit of promising more than his apps deliver, at least so far. He already walked back his pledge to match Adobe's feature set within a month. Developers don't seem to mind the wait: WordCraft had collected more than 12,000 GitHub stars, the platform's version of a bookmark, as of Wednesday.

Before a beta, the roadmap says WordCraft still needs testing against real-world .docx files, charts, and SmartArt that survive a save, page layout closer to Word's, a stability sweep and native printing.

News Bitcoin News Image by CryptoSlate Macro Bearish

Surging dollar forces Bitcoin sell-off as rate hike odds double

Bitcoin faces greater rate risk after September US inflation hit 3.7%, lifting October Fed hike odds to roughly 47% and sending Treasury yields higher.

By Liam 'Akiba' Wright Editor-in-Chief • CryptoSlate

01 September US inflation reached 3.7%, while annual core CPI rose to 2.6%, exceeding the forecasts reported by Reuters. 02 October Fed hike odds near 47% after CPI, compared with roughly 20% before the release. 03 Higher Treasury yields could pressure Bitcoin ahead of the Oct. 27-28 Fed meeting, even if policymakers hold rates. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Bitcoin faces a tougher interest-rate outlook after US inflation data released Oct. 14 pushed bets on another Federal Reserve hike sharply higher. Rising Treasury yields could weigh on Bitcoin by making interest-bearing dollar assets more attractive.

Market-data provider LSEG data shows money markets priced in roughly a 47% chance of another October rate increase after the release, up from closer to 20% beforehand.

September consumer prices were 3.7% higher than a year earlier, up from 3.4% in August, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics release . Annual core inflation, which excludes food and energy, increased to 2.6% from 2.4%. Both readings exceeded forecasts of 3.6% and 2.5%, respectively.

Written by Turner Wright staff writer Edited by Sam Bourgi staff writer Written by Turner Wright staff writer Edited by Sam Bourgi staff writer

Organizations join forces to fight Illinois crypto tax, after 6-month pause

Latest News Published Oct 14, 2026 Illinois officials already agreed to delay implementation of a 0.2% tax on crypto assets, but industry-aligned organizations are pushing for summary judgment on the merits.

The Crypto Council for Innovation (CCI) and Blockchain Association (BA) said they would join the Digital Chamber and others to push for a court to address the merits of a lawsuit over Illinois’s digital-asset tax, set to take effect in 2027.

In a Tuesday filing in the Circuit Court of Sangamon County, the crypto advocacy organizations asked the court to approve an expedited schedule for summary judgment “to reach a decision on the tax’s lawfulness as quickly as possible.” The filing cited the CCI’s and BA’s lawsuit against Illinois state officials, as well as one filed separately by the Digital Chamber and Illinois Blockchain Association.

“While pausing enforcement of the Digital Asset Tax Act protects Illinois consumers and businesses from this onerous and legally flawed tax until July 1, it remains imperative that the merits are determined as soon as possible,” said CCI CEO Ji Kim.

Earlier this month, Illinois officials agreed to delay implementation of the 0.2% crypto tax law for six months, from Jan. 1 to July 1, 2027. The decision, part of the Digital Chamber’s lawsuit, came in response to claims that the digital asset tax had been “slipped into the state’s budget” without debate or public feedback. Digital Chamber CEO Cody Carbone said at the time that the organization would continue with legal proceedings “until this tax is struck down for good.”

Related: French lawmakers back stablecoin swap tax in 2027 budget bill

The expedited schedule, subject to court approval, could allow a decision on the merits of the law by March.

On Friday, Summer Mersinger is scheduled to step down as CEO of the Blockchain Association as part of a leadership transition. Mersinger joined the advocacy group last year after resigning from the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

Kristin Smith, the organization’s former CEO, will step in as interim head, though Mersinger is expected to stay on until the end of 2026.

posts.title: Shayne Coplan Renews Speculation About Polymarket Token
posts.titleVi: Shayne Coplan Renews Speculation About Polymarket Token
posts.summary: Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan has renewed speculation about a native cryptocurrency after discussing an on-chain asset at the just-concluded TOKEN2049 conference in Singapore.
posts.summaryVi: Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan has renewed speculation about a native cryptocurrency after discussing an on-chain asset at the just-concluded TOKEN2049 conference in Singapore.
posts.content:
Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan has renewed speculation about a native cryptocurrency after discussing an on-chain asset at the just-concluded TOKEN2049 conference in Singapore.

However, he offered no launch date or airdrop details, leaving traders guessing whether activity on the prediction market could eventually qualify them for a token allocation.

Coplan’s remarks at TOKEN2049 centered on an asset with “real programmable utility” tied to Polymarket’s platform economy. During a fireside conversation with Balaji Srinivasan, the founder discussed the idea of an on-chain asset but did not confirm a launch, explain how it would work, or specify what holders might receive.

The phrase “real programmable utility” leaves open several possibilities, but Coplan did not outline whether a future token would grant governance rights, provide access to platform functions, or give holders a claim on revenue. He also offered no indication that existing users would automatically qualify for a distribution.

The latest comments follow an earlier hint that drew attention in October last year, when Coplan posted a list of leading cryptocurrencies on X but replaced XRP with “$POLY,” adding a thinking-face emoji, with the cryptic gesture prompting speculation about a Polymarket token.

In that same month, the firm’s Chief Marketing Officer Matthew Modabber indicated that it intended to launch a token and conduct an airdrop. Polymarket’s parent company later filed trademark applications for POLY and $POLY in February 2026, but neither development established that an issuance was imminent.

As of today, Polymarket has not announced a token generation event, published airdrop eligibility requirements or provided a snapshot date or claim instructions, and its existing pUSD collateral token, used for trading on its Polygon-based system, is separate from the proposed POLY asset.

There is also a question of what a token would mean for ordinary traders. A Galaxy Research study published on October 4 examined 2.9 million human-paced Polymarket accounts and found that more than 69% finished below break-even, with combined losses of $338.9 million. The findings concerned the platform’s international operations and tracked wallet addresses rather than verified individual traders.

Meanwhile, a New York lawsuit reported on September 24 alleges that Polymarket’s US operation offered unlicensed gambling and allowed users aged 18 to 20 to trade, despite the state’s minimum age of 21 for mobile sports betting. This is in addition to legal action taken by the city of Baltimore against Polymarket and rival Kalshi for allegedly offering illegal sports betting, and South Korean police opening criminal charges against 26 users of the platform in the country over nearly $13 million in illegal wagers.

His passion for understanding financial systems has led to an intriguing interest in blockchain technology, and he enjoys exploring and writing about cryptocurrencies. Possessing a keen intellect and diligent work ethic, he stays up-to-date on the latest industry trends, regularly sharing his insights in articles and professional presentations.

Kraken moves to acquire $181 million European bank in major push beyond crypto trading

The deal adds to a series of investments in US payments, stablecoin infrastructure and financial services as the company seeks to reduce reliance on external banks.

By Oluwapelumi Adejumo Senior Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 Kraken parent Payward agreed to acquire Lithuania-based Saldo Bank, which held €163 million in assets at the end of 2025. 02 The deal would add €137 million in deposits and a €113.5 million loan book, deepening Payward's expansion beyond crypto trading. 03 The purchase price remains undisclosed, while European regulatory approval is required before the targeted 2027 closing. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Kraken's parent company, Payward, has agreed to acquire a European bank as it expands beyond cryptocurrency trading into traditional financial services.

On Oct. 14, the company announced a definitive agreement to purchase Saldo Finance Oy, a Finnish holding company that owns Lithuania-based Saldo Bank.

The acquisition would give Payward control of a licensed European banking institution with approximately €163 million ($181 million) in assets, offering deposits, lending and payment services across multiple markets.

The transaction, whose financial terms were not disclosed, is expected to close in 2027, subject to regulatory approval.

It marks another step in Payward's effort to build a financial services platform that can handle traditional money and digital assets while reducing its dependence on external banking partners.

Kraken targets European banking expansion with Saldo acquisition

Saldo Bank is an established but relatively small European financial institution whose operations have expanded considerably in recent years.

According to its 2025 audited financial statements , the bank held €162.9 million in assets at the end of December, up about 22% from €133.6 million a year earlier.

Its net loan portfolio increased to €113.5 million from €95.4 million, while retail deposits climbed 24% to €136.9 million.

The bank also reported its first annual profit of approximately €962,000 in 2025, reversing a €2.4 million loss the previous year. Its operating profit before impairment losses rose to €10.4 million, though credit impairment charges absorbed most of it.

These figures show that Payward is acquiring an operating lending business with an established deposit base, although its balance sheet remains modest compared with major European financial institutions.

More importantly, Saldo's existing infrastructure provides a foundation for expanding Payward's financial products across Europe without establishing a new banking operation from scratch.

The institution currently operates in Lithuania, Finland, Sweden, and Germany, and is authorized to expand into the Netherlands. It provides retail term deposits across its operating markets, consumer lending in three countries, and business loans in Lithuania and Finland.

Related Reading Kraken got fed up of waiting on TradFi so it built its own bank to access the Fed — and it just worked

Its credit card business is already operating in Finland, with a Swedish expansion planned for 2027. Saldo also provides embedded lending services that allow fintech companies to offer credit products through its infrastructure.

Payward plans to build on these capabilities by introducing interest-bearing deposits, business and consumer lending, card issuance, and SEPA payment services for European customers.

The acquisition could also support a broader banking-as-a-service business, allowing other financial technology companies to access regulated financial infrastructure through Payward.

Payward co-CEO Arjun Sethi said the transaction forms part of the company's strategy to establish deeper financial relationships with customers. Sethi said:

“We believe whoever owns that relationship earns the right to serve everything around it.”

The strategy builds on Payward's efforts to gain greater control over financial infrastructure.

In March, its Wyoming-chartered subsidiary, Kraken Financial, secured a limited-purpose Federal Reserve master account, providing direct access to US payment infrastructure.

The company also holds an electronic money institution license from the Central Bank of Ireland and says its existing banking operations have originated more than $2 billion in loans.

Meanwhile, Payward expanded its payment capabilities in July by acquiring Reap, a stablecoin-focused company offering card issuance and cross-border transaction infrastructure.

The Saldo acquisition would extend these capabilities into regulated European deposit-taking and lending, potentially allowing Payward to offer banking, cryptocurrency trading and payment services through a more integrated platform.

“We’re not acquiring a bank to be a bank. We’re acquiring the infrastructure to let Payward serve European clients the way a primary financial institution should: one place to hold assets, move them freely, and put them to work.”

European regulatory approval remains key to banking expansion

However, Payward's ability to implement its plans depends on securing regulatory approval and complying with the restrictions attached to Saldo's specialized banking license.

Under Lithuanian banking rules , specialized banks can accept deposits, issue loans, and provide payment services but face restrictions on certain investment activities.

Consequently, ownership of Saldo would not automatically authorize Payward to integrate every cryptocurrency or investment product into the acquired bank.

The transaction will also require supervisory scrutiny of Payward's financial position, management arrangements, and compliance systems.

Beyond regulatory approval, Payward would assume responsibility for maintaining a banking balance sheet, including credit risk, deposit liabilities, and capital requirements.

Saldo's latest financial statements showed total equity of €16.3 million at the end of 2025, with a common equity Tier 1 capital ratio of 14.9% and a total capital adequacy ratio of 19.8%.

These capital measures are key as Payward considers expanding the bank's loan book and other services after the acquisition.

Its credit card business is already operating in Finland, with a Swedish expansion planned for 2027. Saldo also provides embedded lending services that allow fintech companies to offer credit products through its infrastructure.

Payward plans to build on these capabilities by introducing interest-bearing deposits, business and consumer lending, card issuance, and SEPA payment services for European customers.

The acquisition could also support a broader banking-as-a-service business, allowing other financial technology companies to access regulated financial infrastructure through Payward.

Payward co-CEO Arjun Sethi said the transaction forms part of the company's strategy to establish deeper financial relationships with customers. Sethi said:

“We believe whoever owns that relationship earns the right to serve everything around it.”

The strategy builds on Payward's efforts to gain greater control over financial infrastructure.

In March, its Wyoming-chartered subsidiary, Kraken Financial, secured a limited-purpose Federal Reserve master account, providing direct access to US payment infrastructure.

The company also holds an electronic money institution license from the Central Bank of Ireland and says its existing banking operations have originated more than $2 billion in loans.

Meanwhile, Payward expanded its payment capabilities in July by acquiring Reap, a stablecoin-focused company offering card issuance and cross-border transaction infrastructure.

The Saldo acquisition would extend these capabilities into regulated European deposit-taking and lending, potentially allowing Payward to offer banking, cryptocurrency trading and payment services through a more integrated platform.

“We’re not acquiring a bank to be a bank. We’re acquiring the infrastructure to let Payward serve European clients the way a primary financial institution should: one place to hold assets, move them freely, and put them to work.”

European regulatory approval remains key to banking expansion

However, Payward's ability to implement its plans depends on securing regulatory approval and complying with the restrictions attached to Saldo's specialized banking license.

Under Lithuanian banking rules , specialized banks can accept deposits, issue loans, and provide payment services but face restrictions on certain investment activities.

Consequently, ownership of Saldo would not automatically authorize Payward to integrate every cryptocurrency or investment product into the acquired bank.

The transaction will also require supervisory scrutiny of Payward's financial position, management arrangements, and compliance systems.

Beyond regulatory approval, Payward would assume responsibility for maintaining a banking balance sheet, including credit risk, deposit liabilities, and capital requirements.

Saldo's latest financial statements showed total equity of €16.3 million at the end of 2025, with a common equity Tier 1 capital ratio of 14.9% and a total capital adequacy ratio of 19.8%.

These capital measures are key as Payward considers expanding the bank's loan book and other services after the acquisition.

Decrypt News Coins Russia's Biggest Bank Sberbank Wins Approval to Trade Bitcoin

Sberbank now holds both custody and exchange status under Russia's new crypto law, and plans to bring Bitcoin, Ethereum and USDT to apps used by 110 million retail clients.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Moscow, Russia. Image: Shutterstock/Decrypt

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

The Bank of Russia added Sberbank to its register of crypto exchange operators on October 12, six days after listing it as a digital depository.

Sberbank plans to launch its first crypto products on December 1 inside SberBank Online, SberInvestments and SberBusiness, starting with Bitcoin, Ethereum and USDT.

Retail buyers face a 300,000 ruble annual cap per intermediary and a mandatory knowledge test, and paying for goods with crypto remains illegal in Russia.

The Bank of Russia has added Sberbank to its register of organizations authorized to exchange digital currencies, clearing the country's largest lender to buy and sell crypto in its own name and with its own money. The decision was posted on the regulator's website, Russian outlet Interfax reported.

The approval landed six days after the central bank put Sberbank on its separate list of digital depositories, the firms that keep the official record of who owns which coins. Holding both statuses lets the bank sit on the other side of a client's trade and also keep the ledger of that client's holdings, without sending anyone to an outside venue.

Sberbank said the depository status would let it offer crypto services in interfaces clients already use. That means SberBank Online, SberInvestments and SberBusiness, where the bank plans to start with Bitcoin, Ethereum and Tether's USDT on December 1, according to its press service .

The bank has hedged that date, saying it depends on the central bank's decisions and on the secondary regulations being ready in time. Both approvals by the Bank of Russia have now arrived, which leaves the secondary rulebook as the main variable.

Sberbank ended the second quarter with 110.6 million retail clients and 3.5 million corporate clients, per its quarterly results . Plugging crypto into that user base turns a regulated on-ramp into one more menu item inside an app those customers already use for everyday banking.

Deputy Chairman Anatoly Popov has forecast that crypto trading volumes in Russia could reach 4 trillion rubles, roughly $46 billion, in the regime's first year and 7.5 trillion rubles by 2029 or nearly $89.7 billion. The bank also plans to accept Ethereum and USDT, alongside Bitcoin, as collateral for loans once the central bank allows them into public circulation.

Under the law Putin signed in August , non-qualified investors can spend up to 300,000 rubles (about $3,800) a year per intermediary, buyers must pass a knowledge test, and the central bank's draft list of tradable coins includes only Bitcoin, Ethereum, and USDT.

In January 2022, the Bank of Russia proposed banning crypto use, mining and exchanges outright, citing threats to financial stability. Less than five years later, it is licensing the country's biggest lender to run a crypto desk. As of today, spending crypto inside Russia is still illegal, so Sberbank customers will be able to buy Bitcoin but not pay for products with it.

Firms already on the registers have until September 1, 2027, to bring their operations fully in line with the new law, the central bank said .

The Bank of Russia added Sberbank to its register of crypto exchange operators on October 12, six days after listing it as a digital depository.

Sberbank plans to launch its first crypto products on December 1 inside SberBank Online, SberInvestments and SberBusiness, starting with Bitcoin, Ethereum and USDT.

Retail buyers face a 300,000 ruble annual cap per intermediary and a mandatory knowledge test, and paying for goods with crypto remains illegal in Russia.

The Bank of Russia has added Sberbank to its register of organizations authorized to exchange digital currencies, clearing the country's largest lender to buy and sell crypto in its own name and with its own money. The decision was posted on the regulator's website, Russian outlet Interfax reported.

The approval landed six days after the central bank put Sberbank on its separate list of digital depositories, the firms that keep the official record of who owns which coins. Holding both statuses lets the bank sit on the other side of a client's trade and also keep the ledger of that client's holdings, without sending anyone to an outside venue.

Sberbank said the depository status would let it offer crypto services in interfaces clients already use. That means SberBank Online, SberInvestments and SberBusiness, where the bank plans to start with Bitcoin, Ethereum and Tether's USDT on December 1, according to its press service .

The bank has hedged that date, saying it depends on the central bank's decisions and on the secondary regulations being ready in time. Both approvals by the Bank of Russia have now arrived, which leaves the secondary rulebook as the main variable.

Sberbank ended the second quarter with 110.6 million retail clients and 3.5 million corporate clients, per its quarterly results . Plugging crypto into that user base turns a regulated on-ramp into one more menu item inside an app those customers already use for everyday banking.

Deputy Chairman Anatoly Popov has forecast that crypto trading volumes in Russia could reach 4 trillion rubles, roughly $46 billion, in the regime's first year and 7.5 trillion rubles by 2029 or nearly $89.7 billion. The bank also plans to accept Ethereum and USDT, alongside Bitcoin, as collateral for loans once the central bank allows them into public circulation.

Under the law Putin signed in August , non-qualified investors can spend up to 300,000 rubles (about $3,800) a year per intermediary, buyers must pass a knowledge test, and the central bank's draft list of tradable coins includes only Bitcoin, Ethereum, and USDT.

In January 2022, the Bank of Russia proposed banning crypto use, mining and exchanges outright, citing threats to financial stability. Less than five years later, it is licensing the country's biggest lender to run a crypto desk. As of today, spending crypto inside Russia is still illegal, so Sberbank customers will be able to buy Bitcoin but not pay for products with it.

Firms already on the registers have until September 1, 2027, to bring their operations fully in line with the new law, the central bank said .

posts.content:
The world’s leading cryptocurrency exchange announced it will end all services for two digital assets. The actual delisting is scheduled for October 28, but the news has already negatively affected the involved coins.

Additionally, Binance will briefly suspend key operations on the Ethereum (ETH) network to perform wallet maintenance.

The company said it regularly evaluates each listed cryptocurrency to determine whether it continues to meet rigorous criteria and industry standards.

“When a coin or token no longer meets these standards or the industry landscape changes, we conduct a more in-depth review and potentially delist it. Our priority is to ensure the best services and protections for our users while continuing to adapt to evolving market dynamics,” it explained.

Key factors Binance considers include trading volume, adequate liquidity, the team’s commitment to the project, network security against attacks, development activity, and more. Following its latest review, it decided to terminate all services for Epic Chain (EPIC) and QuickSwap (QUICK).

The company will delist the assets from its Copy Trading section on October 21 and remove all spot trading services a week later. After October 29, deposits of these tokens will not be credited to users’ accounts, while withdrawals will be supported until December 28.

Such announcements usually negatively impact the price of the involved cryptocurrencies. After all, Binance remains the largest crypto exchange, and withdrawing support can damage the assets’ reputation, reduce their liquidity, and limit their availability. That said, it is no wonder EPIC plunged 15% in a single day, while QUICK slipped 22%.

Something similar happened in August this year. Back then, Binance delisted Across Protocol (ACX), Hashflow (HFT), PIVX (PIVX), Vulcan Forged PYR (PYR), Vanar (VANRY), and Viction (VIC), triggering double-digit price declines for the affected tokens.

In a separate announcement, Binance revealed that it will perform wallet maintenance for the Ethereum (ETH) network on October 15. To support the process, the exchange will temporarily suspend deposits and withdrawals on that specific blockchain.

The maintenance is expected to take about one hour, after which operations should be resumed. Binance clarified that token trading on the network will not be affected and promised to handle all technical requirements for users.

The company has carried out similar procedures multiple times in recent months, with no reports of major issues.

Decrypt News Technology Solana Sets a Date for Its Next Major Upgrade

Solana's Alpenglow upgrade replaces the TowerBFT voting system on October 21, cutting finality from 12.8 seconds to a target of 150ms and pulling vote transactions out of blocks entirely.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Solana is a smart contract blockchain network. Image: Shutterstock/Decrypt

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Alpenglow activates on Solana mainnet in epoch 1064, which starts on Wednesday, October 21, at approximately 15:00 UTC, according to the Solana Foundation.

The upgrade replaces TowerBFT and targets transaction finality of roughly 150 milliseconds, down from about 12.8 seconds today.

Vote transactions will leave blocks, so Solana's headline transaction counts and TPS figures will drop sharply without any drop in real activity.

Solana has locked in October 21 for Alpenglow, a full replacement of the system its validators use to reach consensus. The switch is tied to epoch 1064, which the Solana Foundation expects to begin around 15:00 UTC that Wednesday.

Alpenglow retires TowerBFT, the current system the network uses, and aims to make transactions final in roughly 150 milliseconds. Finality is the moment a transaction becomes irreversible, and under TowerBFT that currently takes about 12.8 seconds.

On Solana today, a payment is confirmed pretty quickly, but that’s not a guarantee. Until TowerBFT runs out its 13 second clock, the block could in theory still be dropped.

That small doubt is why anyone handling real money tends to wait out the full window. With finality at around 150ms, the irreversible answer arrives almost as fast as the optimistic one, which is what a checkout counter taking SOL or a DeFI application, or a trading desk settling a position actually needs.

TowerBFT works by having validators post their votes as on-chain transactions, and a block only counts as final once 32 slots’ worth of those votes pile up. Votor, the voting protocol shipping with Alpenglow, takes votes off the chain, so validators message each other directly, package the votes into certificates, and can lock in a block after a single round of voting, or two at most.

When 80% or more of stake backs a block in the first round, it finalizes on the spot. If support lands between 60% and 80%, a second round with 60% thresholds decides whether the block is finalized or skipped, and the Foundation says the design tolerates 20% malicious stake plus another 20% offline.

Alpenglow goes live on mainnet-beta Wednesday, October 21, ~14:50 UTC.

18 months of work for a migration that happens in one slot. Finality drops from seconds to ~150ms.

Make sure to 

Ordinary users don’t need to do anything, and wallets and apps should behave as they do now. The Solana Virtual Machine, transaction formats, programs, and fees are left alone, while for developers the “confirmed” and “finalized” commitment levels become one and the same.

Each vote account also needs 0.8 SOL on top of its rent-exempt balance to pay the new Validator Admission Ticket, a per-epoch fee of the same size that gets burned. It replaces the roughly 1 SOL per epoch validators spent on vote transaction fees under TowerBFT, and a validator that can’t cover it sits out voting and block production for the following epoch.

The feature gate turns on as epoch 1064 begins, yet TowerBFT stays in charge for another 5,000 slots, roughly 18 minutes, before Alpenglow takes control at slot 459,653,000. This assures stability and prevents any issues during transition.

Validators approved Alpenglow in September 2025, when the SIMD-0326 proposal passed with 98.27% of votes cast in favor. In May, Anza Lead Economist Max Resnick told Decrypt the team was looking at a late Q3 or early Q4 mainnet activation, so everything is going according to schedule.

October 21 delivers only Votor, the first half of Alpenglow. Rotor, a replacement for Turbine, the system Solana uses to broadcast block data between validators, comes later and still has no date.

Decrypt News Technology Solana Sets a Date for Its Next Major Upgrade

Solana's Alpenglow upgrade replaces the TowerBFT voting system on October 21, cutting finality from 12.8 seconds to a target of 150ms and pulling vote transactions out of blocks entirely.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Solana is a smart contract blockchain network. Image: Shutterstock/Decrypt

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Alpenglow activates on Solana mainnet in epoch 1064, which starts on Wednesday, October 21, at approximately 15:00 UTC, according to the Solana Foundation.

The upgrade replaces TowerBFT and targets transaction finality of roughly 150 milliseconds, down from about 12.8 seconds today.

Vote transactions will leave blocks, so Solana's headline transaction counts and TPS figures will drop sharply without any drop in real activity.

Solana has locked in October 21 for Alpenglow, a full replacement of the system its validators use to reach consensus. The switch is tied to epoch 1064, which the Solana Foundation expects to begin around 15:00 UTC that Wednesday.

Alpenglow retires TowerBFT, the current system the network uses, and aims to make transactions final in roughly 150 milliseconds. Finality is the moment a transaction becomes irreversible, and under TowerBFT that currently takes about 12.8 seconds.

On Solana today, a payment is confirmed pretty quickly, but that’s not a guarantee. Until TowerBFT runs out its 13 second clock, the block could in theory still be dropped.

That small doubt is why anyone handling real money tends to wait out the full window. With finality at around 150ms, the irreversible answer arrives almost as fast as the optimistic one, which is what a checkout counter taking SOL or a DeFI application, or a trading desk settling a position actually needs.

TowerBFT works by having validators post their votes as on-chain transactions, and a block only counts as final once 32 slots’ worth of those votes pile up. Votor, the voting protocol shipping with Alpenglow, takes votes off the chain, so validators message each other directly, package the votes into certificates, and can lock in a block after a single round of voting, or two at most.

When 80% or more of stake backs a block in the first round, it finalizes on the spot. If support lands between 60% and 80%, a second round with 60% thresholds decides whether the block is finalized or skipped, and the Foundation says the design tolerates 20% malicious stake plus another 20% offline.

Alpenglow goes live on mainnet-beta Wednesday, October 21, ~14:50 UTC.

18 months of work for a migration that happens in one slot. Finality drops from seconds to ~150ms.

Make sure to 

Ordinary users don’t need to do anything, and wallets and apps should behave as they do now. The Solana Virtual Machine, transaction formats, programs, and fees are left alone, while for developers the “confirmed” and “finalized” commitment levels become one and the same.

Each vote account also needs 0.8 SOL on top of its rent-exempt balance to pay the new Validator Admission Ticket, a per-epoch fee of the same size that gets burned. It replaces the roughly 1 SOL per epoch validators spent on vote transaction fees under TowerBFT, and a validator that can’t cover it sits out voting and block production for the following epoch.

The feature gate turns on as epoch 1064 begins, yet TowerBFT stays in charge for another 5,000 slots, roughly 18 minutes, before Alpenglow takes control at slot 459,653,000. This assures stability and prevents any issues during transition.

Validators approved Alpenglow in September 2025, when the SIMD-0326 proposal passed with 98.27% of votes cast in favor. In May, Anza Lead Economist Max Resnick told Decrypt the team was looking at a late Q3 or early Q4 mainnet activation, so everything is going according to schedule.

October 21 delivers only Votor, the first half of Alpenglow. Rotor, a replacement for Turbine, the system Solana uses to broadcast block data between validators, comes later and still has no date.

Written by Turner Wright staff writer Edited by Sam Bourgi staff writer Written by Turner Wright staff writer Edited by Sam Bourgi staff writer

EU authority classifies Circle’s USDC as ‘significant’ under MiCA

Latest News Published Oct 14, 2026 The second-largest stablecoin by market cap will be overseen by French and EU authorities under its classification as a “significant e-money token.“

The European Banking Authority (EBA) has classified Circle’s USDC stablecoin as a significant e-money token under the region’s Markets in Crypto Assets (MiCA) framework.

In a Wednesday notice, the banking regulator said the e-money token classification, granted to only 45 other projects, effectively means the USDC stablecoin will be jointly overseen by the EBA and France’s supervisory authority, the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution. The stablecoin is the second largest by market capitalization, at $73 billion compared to Tether USDt’s $184 billion.

The “significant“ classification came as many EU-based token issuers pushed for regulated US dollar-pegged stablecoins in the region. Stable Mint CEO James Bennett told Cointelegraph that while Europe couldn’t “wish away“ dollar stablecoins, regulators could control safeguards and rules for issuers.

“For European corporates to make cross-border payments globally, offering only a euro stablecoin isn’t enough,” AllUnity CEO Alexander Höptner told Cointelegraph.

As authorities and issuers move closer to embracing dollar stablecoins, policymakers at the European Central Bank continue to explore the potential introduction of a digital euro. The EU authority first proposed the central bank digital currency in 2020, with the potential to issue the coin in 2029 after the conclusion of legislation and a pilot program.

Ripple targets trillion-dollar securities markets with new US brokerage and South Korean deals

The partnerships extend Ripple's infrastructure into stock-market settlement and securities tokenization, although commercial deployments remain at different stages.

By Oluwapelumi Adejumo Senior Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 Ripple secured partnerships with DriveWealth and Meritz Securities to expand its stablecoin, custody and tokenization services into global capital markets. 02 The agreements could bring RLUSD into brokerage settlement while expanding Ripple's reach across South Korea's regulated securities industry. 03 The partnerships open new commercial opportunities, but neither announcement establishes revenue expectations or a complete deployment timetable. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Ripple announced partnerships with DriveWealth and Meritz Securities to extend its services across global brokerage and securities markets.

The two agreements, announced on Oct. 14 , will bring Ripple's stablecoin, payments, and custody infrastructure into DriveWealth's brokerage operations while exploring securities tokenization opportunities with South Korea's Meritz.

DriveWealth, which provides investment infrastructure to more than 100 partners worldwide, plans to integrate Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin into European settlement operations, with potential expansion into the US. Meanwhile, Meritz becomes Ripple's first Korean securities-firm partner and fourth institutional partner in the country this year.

Related Reading Standard Chartered brings Ripple's RLUSD into banking custody after $765 million quarterly surge

The agreements deepen Ripple's expansion beyond cross-border payments into traditional capital markets, where financial institutions are exploring blockchain technology to reduce settlement delays, manage collateral and tokenize financial assets.

They also come as South Korea prepares to introduce a regulatory framework for tokenized securities in February 2027, potentially opening another market for Ripple's institutional infrastructure.

DriveWealth brings RLUSD into global brokerage infrastructure

Under the DriveWealth agreement, the brokerage infrastructure provider will integrate RLUSD on the XRP Ledger to support settlement in Europe, alongside Ripple's stablecoin issuance and redemption capabilities.

The integration addresses a longstanding challenge in international investing: stock trading has become increasingly accessible outside conventional market hours, while the banking infrastructure used to fund transactions still operates under geographic and time restrictions.

DriveWealth already supports trading in US equities for 24 hours a day, five days a week. However, international clients can face delays when moving funds across borders, particularly when transfers depend on bank operating hours.

The companies intend to let clients fund and manage collateral accounts with stablecoins that can be converted to cash in near real time, potentially reducing the capital held idle while awaiting traditional bank transfers.

“We've already enabled 24/5 trading; now we need the funding to match,” DriveWealth Chief Executive Officer Naureen Hassan said in the announcement.

The partnership extends beyond stablecoin settlement.

DriveWealth will integrate Ripple Payments to support cross-border funding from its international partners and use Ripple's digital-asset custody infrastructure in Europe, with plans to expand into additional markets.

The companies are also exploring equity financing opportunities through Ripple Prime's Delta One business, which covers institutional services involving US equities and equity derivatives.

For Ripple, the arrangement creates an opportunity to distribute its infrastructure through DriveWealth's existing brokerage network, which serves financial institutions, digital wallets and fintech platforms offering access to US markets.

However, the companies did not disclose expected settlement volumes, financial terms or a timetable for completing every integration.

South Korea deal expands Ripple's institutional reach

Ripple's separate agreement with Meritz Securities extends that capital-markets strategy into South Korea, where financial institutions are preparing for the introduction of regulated tokenized securities.

The companies will initially explore Ripple Custody and tokenization infrastructure within Meritz's existing securities operations, expanding their cooperation as the country's digital-asset regulations develop.

Meritz is evaluating opportunities involving fractional investment products, security tokens, trading platforms, spot exchange-traded funds and won-denominated stablecoins. The agreement does not commit either company to launching those products.

The partnership adds a securities firm to Ripple's growing Korean institutional network , following earlier agreements with Kyobo Life Insurance, Kbank and Jeonbuk Bank.

Those relationships cover tokenized government-bond settlement, digital-asset custody wallets and cross-border remittances, respectively, giving Ripple connections across several functions of the country's financial system.

The latest expansion comes ahead of a major regulatory change.

South Korea's Financial Services Commission has scheduled the first phase of its tokenized-securities framework to begin on Feb. 4, 2027, when amendments to the Electronic Registration Act take effect.

The initial phase will cover selected institutional bonds and money market funds, unlisted shares issued through trust structures and certain fractional investment securities. Broader public securities and stablecoin-linked settlement infrastructure are planned for later stages.

The framework could create opportunities for custody and tokenization providers as securities firms develop systems to issue, record, and transfer blockchain-based financial instruments.

posts.title: Coinbase Lays Out Post-Quantum Needs for Bitcoin Custody
posts.titleVi: Coinbase Lays Out Post-Quantum Needs for Bitcoin Custody
posts.summary: Coinbase, the custodian holding about 5% of all BTC, published a technical blog on October 13 outlining what it wants from Bitcoin’s move to quantum-resistant security.
posts.summaryVi: Coinbase, the custodian holding about 5% of all BTC, published a technical blog on October 13 outlining what it wants from Bitcoin’s move to quantum-resistant security.
posts.content:
Coinbase, the custodian holding about 5% of all BTC, published a technical blog on October 13 outlining what it wants from Bitcoin’s move to quantum-resistant security.

Its central point is that choosing a new digital signature scheme is only one piece of the job, since any plan also has to fit Bitcoin’s scarce block space and work for custodians and everyday wallets.

In the blog post, the exchange said it is already preparing its own systems, convening talks with Bitcoin developers and backing open-source work through the Bitcoin Security Consortium.

The company pointed to P2MR, proposed in BIP-360, and P2TRv2 as possible output designs that could accommodate future post-quantum signature systems without requiring a complete redesign each time the cryptography changes.

It also proposed evaluating hybrid arrangements in which a wallet could spend funds through either a conventional ECDSA/Schnorr signature or a post-quantum key during the transition.

Coinbase raised particular concerns about stateful post-quantum signatures. Although these schemes can be smaller and faster than stateless alternatives, reusing signing state can make forgery possible. The company warned that recovering from failed updates or lost state could be difficult for exchanges running multiple signing servers, as well as individuals managing their own wallets.

Its suggested evaluation criteria include signature size, verification speed, transaction fees, full-node workload, hardware wallet compatibility, and multi-party computation, or MPC, which allows parties to produce signatures without relying on one complete private key held in a single place. Coinbase also named ML-DSA, the prospective FN-DSA standard, and SHRINCS as candidates for assessment.

Wallets that migrate late are the last open item. If Bitcoin eventually limits or ends ECDSA and Schnorr spending, Coinbase wondered whether and how those users could move funds afterward.

The issue is already being considered, with BIP-361, fronted by Jameson Lopp and five other developers, proposing to first restrict sending to quantum-vulnerable addresses and later stop old-style signatures from spending, with an unconfirmed third phase that might let people recover funds after a missed deadline.

The plan has drawn objections that protocol-level freezes cut against censorship resistance and self-responsibility for funds. But in April, BitMEX Research floated a “canary” alternative, where a freeze would trigger only if funds leave a special address whose private key nobody knows, since such a spend would prove a quantum computer exists.

Coinbase, the custodian holding about 5% of all BTC, published a technical blog on October 13 outlining what it wants from Bitcoin’s move to quantum-resistant security.

Its central point is that choosing a new digital signature scheme is only one piece of the job, since any plan also has to fit Bitcoin’s scarce block space and work for custodians and everyday wallets.

In the blog post, the exchange said it is already preparing its own systems, convening talks with Bitcoin developers and backing open-source work through the Bitcoin Security Consortium.

The company pointed to P2MR, proposed in BIP-360, and P2TRv2 as possible output designs that could accommodate future post-quantum signature systems without requiring a complete redesign each time the cryptography changes.

It also proposed evaluating hybrid arrangements in which a wallet could spend funds through either a conventional ECDSA/Schnorr signature or a post-quantum key during the transition.

Coinbase raised particular concerns about stateful post-quantum signatures. Although these schemes can be smaller and faster than stateless alternatives, reusing signing state can make forgery possible. The company warned that recovering from failed updates or lost state could be difficult for exchanges running multiple signing servers, as well as individuals managing their own wallets.

Its suggested evaluation criteria include signature size, verification speed, transaction fees, full-node workload, hardware wallet compatibility, and multi-party computation, or MPC, which allows parties to produce signatures without relying on one complete private key held in a single place. Coinbase also named ML-DSA, the prospective FN-DSA standard, and SHRINCS as candidates for assessment.

Wallets that migrate late are the last open item. If Bitcoin eventually limits or ends ECDSA and Schnorr spending, Coinbase wondered whether and how those users could move funds afterward.

The issue is already being considered, with BIP-361, fronted by Jameson Lopp and five other developers, proposing to first restrict sending to quantum-vulnerable addresses and later stop old-style signatures from spending, with an unconfirmed third phase that might let people recover funds after a missed deadline.

The plan has drawn objections that protocol-level freezes cut against censorship resistance and self-responsibility for funds. But in April, BitMEX Research floated a “canary” alternative, where a freeze would trigger only if funds leave a special address whose private key nobody knows, since such a spend would prove a quantum computer exists.

US authorities dismantle crypto scam network that stole tens of millions

Latest News Published Oct 14, 2026 Brooklyn prosecutors and the FBI seized 112 servers and shut down 241 websites linked to investment scams that targeted Russian-speaking Americans.

Prosecutors in Brooklyn, New York, working with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), have disrupted an Eastern European cryptocurrency scam network accused of stealing tens of millions of dollars from Americans, primarily Russian-speakers.

The operation, carried out last week and announced on Wednesday, resulted in the shutdown of 241 websites and the seizure of 112 servers hosted by companies in Eastern Europe and the United States, according to the Brooklyn District Attorney’s Office. No arrests were made.

“These criminals stole many millions of dollars from Russian-speaking victims through an elaborate investment scheme, then tried to exploit them again with false promises to recover their money,” Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez said in a statement. He credited the office’s Virtual Currency Unit and the FBI with uncovering the network’s infrastructure.

Seizing the servers was key to the operation because it disrupted the scammers’ ability to create new websites and contact victims. “We disabled the back end of the operation,” Assistant District Attorney Alona Katz, who led the investigation, said , according to Bloomberg.

The operation comes amid a rise in cryptocurrency-related fraud across the US. Americans reported $11.4 billion in crypto fraud losses in 2025, a 22% increase from the previous year, according to FBI figures cited by Bloomberg.

Ethereum’s quantum race takes a new turn as zkSync courts banks and Starknet weighs exit

zkSync's new prover meets Ethereum's real-time performance benchmark while rival Starknet considers independence, highlighting diverging paths for L2 networks

By Gino Matos Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 zkSync unveiled a real-time Ethereum prover as Starknet considers becoming an independent blockchain to accelerate quantum protection. 02 The competing strategies highlight how Ethereum's quantum-security roadmap is reshaping priorities across its Layer-2 ecosystem. 03 zkSync is courting banks while Starknet weighs independence, but neither strategy has established a sustainable commercial model. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

ZkSync announced Airbender Prime, a prover that Matter Labs says handled 99% of 7,200 consecutive Ethereum mainnet blocks in under 10 seconds each on a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU.

The announcement came five days after Starknet said it is actively considering becoming an independent layer-1 (L1) blockchain, targeting full quantum resistance in 2027.

The two announcements answer the same deadline from opposite directions, since Ethereum's own target for L1 quantum resistance across execution, consensus, and data is December 2029.

A prover that meets the real-time benchmark

The Ethereum Foundation defines real-time proving as 99% of mainnet blocks proven in 10 seconds or less, which fits Ethereum's 12-second slot and propagation assumptions .

ZkSync's result maps to that definition, including witness preparation, with every block finishing in under 12 seconds.

Airbender Prime uses hash-based STARKs that combine GKR sumcheck, WHIR polynomial commitments, and BLAKE2s hashing, with Keccak-256-based commitments for L1 proofs replacing BN254 pairings.

Nvidia rates the card at 600 watts of board power, and marketplace reporting puts it near $16,000. The Foundation's target framework also covers proof sizes under 300 KiB, a long-term 128-bit security level, on-premise capital spending near $100,000, and power draw under 10 kilowatts.

Full-system electricity use, proof sizes and long-term operating costs for Prime await independent measurement, and the Foundation's public proving program continues to evaluate security and reliability.

Ethereum's ECDSA account signatures, BLS validator signatures and KZG data commitments belong to separate protocol-level work, and the December 2029 target stands as published, a schedule the Foundation calls aggressive. The prover operates outside Ethereum's consensus protocol .

Quantum preparation arrives while standalone chains struggle to pay their way. Blast set an Oct. 26 user-exit deadline, saying maintenance costs exceeded revenue, and Abstract is shutting down.

Aave's risk provider LlamaRisk recommended winding down V3 deployments on six chains, including zkSync, saying zkSync, Scroll and Sonic each generated less than $5,000 in quarterly protocol revenue at current balances.

Related Reading Starknet considers leaving Ethereum for a quantum-resistant Layer 1

The evidence points to consolidation and specialization, and many layer-2 (L2) blockchains keep operating. Cheap execution earns too little on its own, and liquidity, distribution, compliance, and institutional access are becoming the defensible layers.

Starknet's proving layer already rests on hash functions, according to StarkWare's June roadmap, with its Ethereum dependencies sitting in bridge messaging and blob data availability.

Becoming an L1 would bring those surfaces under Starknet's control and let it set its own timeline. The idea remains under consideration and would need governance approval and engineering execution.

ZkSync is investing in technology useful to Ethereum's own architecture and pointing its commercial effort at regulated finance. Starknet explores independence from the base layer, and zkSync builds components for it.

Matter Labs' third-quarter report says it prioritized private institutional interoperability over public Gateway interoperability.

Institutions building on its Prividium platform asked for private execution, direct Ethereum settlement, and atomic transfers between Prividium chains. The report removed the interop fees from the original public Gateway proposal and lists the private-interoperability fee model as ongoing work.

Matter Labs says Deutsche Bundesbank is testing Prividium's open-source permissioning engine in its own infrastructure, which lets regulated institutions run and inspect core code themselves.

The Cari case study from zkSync describes five founding US regional bank partners holding more than $8 trillion in assets. A zkSync-hosted summary puts the broader network at more than 30 institutions with over $10 trillion in combined assets.

Any link between Prividium usage and ZK token demand awaits a published fee model.

If Airbender Prime and similar systems keep meeting the Foundation's security, cost, proof-size, and on-premise targets, zkSync could supply proof infrastructure for Ethereum's route toward independently verifiable execution while Prividium pilots grow into fee-paying deployments.

That path gives former L2 teams a role as suppliers to the base layer and to regulated finance.

If Prividium deployments remain pilots, private-interoperability fees stay unfinished and public zkSync activity stays weak, the market reads zkSync as a prover stack with a technical result and a thin commercial one.

A compressed quantum timeline would add urgency to Starknet's L1 option and push Ethereum to accelerate its account, consensus, and data-layer migrations.

Ethereum's quantum preparations and its scaling sector are being restructured together, and each L2 team is picking among a sovereign chain, a supplier role to Ethereum, a bank-grade vendor business, or consolidation.

Written by Turner Wright staff writer Edited by Robert Lakin staff editor Written by Turner Wright staff writer Edited by Robert Lakin staff editor

OCC report finds debanking efforts tied to crypto activities

Latest News Published Oct 14, 2026 The report from the US banking regulator did not include specific examples of debanking related to crypto, but mentioned it alongside ties to oil, gas and firearms.

The US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) released a report on debanking efforts, including ties to digital assets as activities that influenced banks to limit financial services.

In a report released Wednesday, the OCC said certain banks had “public and nonpublic policies” restricting services for many industries, including oil and gas, tobacco, firearms and digital assets. According to the banking regulator, the report was in accordance with an August 2025 executive order from US President Donald Trump to prevent what he called “unlawful debanking.”

“Many institutions also placed restrictions on banking digital asset activities, including on issuers, exchanges, or administrators, often attributed to financial crime considerations,” said the OCC.

In November 2024, more than 30 tech and crypto executives claimed to have been denied access to banking services. Many in the crypto industry unofficially dubbed the effort as “Operation Chokepoint 2.0” after the Obama-era initiative to fight fraud and money laundering facilitated by banks.

However, Wednesday’s 47-page report did not include specific examples of debanking relating to digital asset activities. The OCC said it had been “unable to quantify on a comprehensive basis the full extent of debanking or alleged debanking actions” based on a review of nine major banks, and the agency’s head, Jonathan Gould, focused largely on the report’s claims around debanking due to ties to coal and firearms.

“These decisions were not based on financial risk,” said Gould, referencing the debanking due to connections to coal. “Instead, banks cited concerns about negative headlines, public protests, and the perceived reputational consequences of supporting the industry.”

The 2025 executive order from Trump followed calls from many in the industry surrounding claims -- including “Operation Chokepoint 2.0” -- that the US government under former President Joe Biden may have influenced financial institutions into cutting off crypto firms from certain services.

Báo cáo CPI của Mỹ hôm nay: Kỳ vọng lạm phát tháng 9 và tác động đến thị trường

Báo cáo CPI tháng 9 của Mỹ dự kiến ​​được công bố vào ngày 14 tháng 10 lúc 8:30 sáng giờ ET (6:00 chiều giờ IST). Dữ liệu này có thể ảnh hưởng đến kỳ vọng của thị trường về quyết định lãi suất tiếp theo của Cục Dự trữ Liên bang và gây ra biến động trên thị trường chứng khoán, vàng và bạc.

Các nhà kinh tế dự báo lạm phát chung sẽ tăng lên 3,6% so với cùng kỳ năm ngoái, từ mức 3,4% trong tháng 8, chủ yếu do giá năng lượng tăng cao.

Chỉ số CPI tổng thể so với cùng kỳ năm trước: 3,6%, tăng từ 3,4% trong tháng 8. Chỉ số CPI tổng thể hàng tháng: 0,6%, so với 0,4% trong tháng 8. Chỉ số CPI cốt lõi so với cùng kỳ năm trước: 2,5%, tăng từ 2,4% trong tháng 8. Chỉ số CPI cốt lõi hàng tháng: Dự kiến ​​0,2%. Chỉ số CPI cốt lõi không bao gồm giá thực phẩm và năng lượng. Các nhà đầu tư sẽ theo dõi con số này để đánh giá xem lạm phát có đang gia tăng vượt quá tác động của chi phí năng lượng cao hơn hay không.

Chỉ số CPI có thể ảnh hưởng đến thị trường chứng khoán như thế nào?

Phản ứng của thị trường sẽ phụ thuộc vào việc số liệu lạm phát thực tế cao hơn, thấp hơn hay đúng với kỳ vọng.

Lạm phát thấp hơn dự kiến: Lạm phát thấp hơn có thể làm giảm bớt lo ngại về áp lực giá cả dai dẳng, có khả năng làm giảm lợi suất trái phiếu kho bạc và làm suy yếu đồng đô la Mỹ. Điều này có thể hỗ trợ thị trường chứng khoán và các tài sản rủi ro khác. Lạm phát phù hợp với kỳ vọng: Thị trường có thể tập trung vào lạm phát lõi và liệu giá năng lượng tăng cao có phải là nguyên nhân chính dẫn đến sự gia tăng chỉ số CPI tổng thể hay không. Lạm phát vượt dự báo: Chỉ số lạm phát cao hơn có thể làm mạnh đồng đô la và đẩy lợi suất trái phiếu kho bạc lên cao. Các nhà đầu tư có thể giảm kỳ vọng về việc Cục Dự trữ Liên bang cắt giảm lãi suất, gây áp lực lên thị trường chứng khoán. Chỉ số CPI tổng thể cao hơn không nhất thiết có nghĩa là lạm phát đang gia tăng trên toàn nền kinh tế. CPI cốt lõi sẽ giúp các nhà đầu tư đánh giá xem áp lực giá cả có đang lan rộng ra ngoài lĩnh vực năng lượng hay không.

Vì sao đồng đô la Mỹ và lợi suất trái phiếu kho bạc lại quan trọng?

Theo các nguồn tin thị trường, chỉ số đô la Mỹ (DXY) đã đạt mức 102,58, mức cao nhất trong 18 tháng, sau khi tăng khoảng 3,5% trong một tháng.

Đồng đô la mạnh hơn và lợi suất trái phiếu kho bạc cao hơn có thể gây áp lực lên cổ phiếu và các tài sản rủi ro khác. Lạm phát thấp hơn có thể làm giảm bớt lo ngại về lãi suất và mang lại sự ổn định cho thị trường.

Câu hỏi then chốt là liệu báo cáo CPI tháng 9 có làm thay đổi kỳ vọng về quyết định lãi suất tiếp theo của Cục Dự trữ Liên bang hay không.

Các nhà đầu tư cũng sẽ theo dõi các thông tin và sự kiện kinh tế sau đây:

Ngày 15 tháng 10: Chỉ số giá sản xuất (PPI) và dữ liệu doanh số bán lẻ của Mỹ. Ngày 16 tháng 10: Chủ tịch Cục Dự trữ Liên bang Kevin Warsh dự kiến ​​sẽ phát biểu. Ngày 27-28 tháng 10: Cuộc họp của Cục Dự trữ Liên bang. Chỉ số giá sản xuất (PPI) sẽ cung cấp thêm một dấu hiệu về áp lực giá cả ở cấp độ nhà sản xuất, trong khi dữ liệu doanh số bán lẻ sẽ cho thấy nhu cầu của người tiêu dùng.

Báo cáo CPI tháng 9 có thể ảnh hưởng đến hướng đi của thị trường trước cuộc họp tháng 10 của Cục Dự trữ Liên bang, đặc biệt nếu lạm phát khác với dự kiến.

posts.content:
Payward mua lại Saldo Bank để mở rộng dịch vụ ngân hàng tiền điện tử tại châu Âu

Payward, công ty mẹ của Kraken, đã đồng ý mua lại Saldo Bank, một ngân hàng được cấp phép hoạt động tại Liên minh Châu Âu. Thỏa thuận này sẽ cho phép Payward kết hợp giao dịch tiền điện tử với tiền gửi ngân hàng, cho vay, thanh toán thẻ và các dịch vụ tín dụng.

Trong khi đó, thương vụ mua lại Saldo dự kiến ​​sẽ hoàn tất vào năm 2027, tùy thuộc vào sự chấp thuận của cơ quan quản lý.

Payward có kế hoạch kết hợp ngân hàng và tiền điện tử

Trong một thông cáo báo chí ngày 14 tháng 10, Payward thông báo rằng họ đã ký kết thỏa thuận cuối cùng để mua lại Saldo Bank, một ngân hàng có trụ sở tại Lithuania được cấp phép hoạt động tại Liên minh Châu Âu.

Saldo được Ngân hàng Trung ương Châu Âu cấp phép và chịu sự giám sát của Ngân hàng Lithuania. Công ty hoạt động tại Lithuania, Phần Lan, Thụy Điển và Đức, và cũng có thể phục vụ khách hàng tại Hà Lan.

Thỏa thuận này sẽ cho phép Payward cung cấp các dịch vụ ngân hàng truyền thống, bao gồm tiền gửi, cho vay và thanh toán thẻ, cùng với các dịch vụ tiền điện tử hiện có. Điều này sẽ mang đến cho khách hàng nhiều cách hơn để quản lý tiền và tài sản kỹ thuật số của họ thông qua một nền tảng duy nhất.

Nếu được chấp thuận, thương vụ này sẽ đánh dấu lần đầu tiên một công ty quản lý tài sản kỹ thuật số mua lại một ngân hàng thương mại tại châu Âu.

Khách hàng có thể vay tiền dựa trên số tiền điện tử đang nắm giữ mà không cần bán chúng

Một trong những lợi ích chính của thương vụ mua lại này là khả năng vay tiền mặt dựa trên việc nắm giữ tiền điện tử hoặc cổ phiếu được mã hóa. Khách hàng tổ chức có thể sử dụng các tài sản này làm tài sản thế chấp mà không cần bán cổ phần của mình để tiếp cận nguồn vốn.

Đồng Giám đốc điều hành của Payward, Arjun Sethi, cho biết khách hàng đã yêu cầu tính năng này. Ông cũng giải thích lý do tại sao giấy phép ngân hàng lại quan trọng đối với kế hoạch dài hạn của công ty.

“Bất cứ ai có quyền gửi tiền, cho vay và phát hành các công cụ thanh toán cho khách hàng đều nắm giữ mối quan hệ đó.”

Ông nói thêm rằng các hoạt động giao dịch, đặt cược, quản lý tài sản và dịch vụ kho bạc có thể được xây dựng trên nền tảng đó.

Payward mở rộng hoạt động ngoài lĩnh vực giao dịch tiền điện tử

Thương vụ Saldo diễn ra sau khi Payward được cho là đã mua lại sàn giao dịch phái sinh Bitnomial với giá 550 triệu đô la và thâu tóm công ty thanh toán stablecoin Reap Technologies với giá 600 triệu đô la. Cả hai động thái này cho thấy sự bành trướng của công ty vào lĩnh vực giao dịch được quản lý, thanh toán và cơ sở hạ tầng ngân hàng.

Việc mở rộng này cũng diễn ra trong bối cảnh các tổ chức tài chính truyền thống đang tìm cách tăng cường hợp tác với Payward. Các báo cáo cho thấy Wells Fargo đang đàm phán với công ty này về việc cung cấp các dịch vụ thanh khoản giao dịch tiền điện tử cốt lõi.

Việc mua lại Saldo dự kiến ​​sẽ hoàn tất vào năm 2027, tùy thuộc vào sự chấp thuận của cơ quan quản lý.

posts.content:
Liệu Bitcoin có giảm xuống còn 75.000 USD? Tại sao mức giá vốn Saylor là mức cần theo dõi?

Hai người mua Bitcoin lớn nhất đều rút lui vào tuần trước. Các quỹ ETF Bitcoin giao ngay của Mỹ ghi nhận dòng tiền chảy ra lớn nhất trong gần bốn tháng, và Strategy của Michael Saylor đã thực hiện giao dịch mua Bitcoin nhỏ nhất trong năm.

Tuy nhiên, Bitcoin vẫn giữ vững trên mức 80.000 đô la trong suốt một tuần. Một nhà phân tích đã xem xét kỹ lưỡng dữ liệu để tìm ra ai vẫn đang mua vào.

Bitcoin đã bị từ chối ở mức kháng cự vào thứ Hai sau khi đạt mốc 84.352 đô la, sau đó giảm xuống khoảng 81.000 đô la trong đêm. Kể từ đó, nó đã bật tăng trở lại trên 83.000 đô la. Mức thấp nhất của tuần trước, vào ngày 8 tháng 10, là 80.393 đô la. Bitcoin đã giảm khoảng 4% so với đầu tuần. Các quỹ ETF Bitcoin giao ngay đã mất 679 triệu đô la trong tuần trước, tương đương khoảng 8.000 BTC theo giá hiện tại.

Kể từ khi ra mắt vào tháng 1 năm 2024, các quỹ ETF đã thu hút được tổng cộng 57 tỷ đô la, vì vậy dòng tiền chảy ra tuần trước chỉ chiếm khoảng 1,2% tổng số đó. Lợi suất trái phiếu cao hơn có thể giải thích một phần nguyên nhân của việc bán ra. Lợi suất trái phiếu kho bạc Mỹ kỳ hạn 10 năm đã đóng cửa ở mức 5,31% vào thứ Hai tuần trước, mức cao nhất trong năm, mang đến cho các nhà đầu tư một lựa chọn an toàn hơn.

Ông cũng so sánh tình hình hiện tại với giai đoạn tồi tệ hơn nhiều hồi đầu năm. Từ giữa tháng 5 đến đầu tháng 7, các quỹ ETF chứng kiến ​​tám tuần liên tiếp dòng tiền chảy ra với tổng cộng khoảng 8,3 tỷ đô la, gấp hơn 12 lần con số của tuần trước. Bitcoin đã giảm từ khoảng 80.700 đô la xuống dưới 59.000 đô la trong giai đoạn đó, giảm hơn 25%. Các quỹ ETF cũng ghi nhận dòng tiền chảy ra trong khoảng một nửa số ngày giao dịch trong năm nay, điều mà ông cho là bình thường.

Strategy chỉ mua 250 BTC với giá 21,5 triệu đô la Mỹ từ ngày 5 đến 11 tháng 10, đây là giao dịch mua nhỏ nhất của họ trong năm 2026. Cùng tuần đó, họ đã chi 192,4 triệu đô la Mỹ để mua lại cổ phiếu ưu đãi STRC của chính mình, gần gấp chín lần số tiền họ đã đầu tư vào Bitcoin.

Hiện tại, công ty đang nắm giữ 848.250 BTC với giá trị trung bình là 75.444 đô la.

Phần lớn hoạt động bán ra đến từ các nhà giao dịch sử dụng đòn bẩy. Trên Binance, khối lượng hợp đồng mở (open interest) của hợp đồng tương lai Bitcoin đã giảm từ khoảng 97.400 BTC xuống còn khoảng 92.400 BTC trong tuần, giảm khoảng 5%. Lãi suất cho phép (funding rate) đã giảm xuống gần bằng 0, cho thấy lượng đòn bẩy dư thừa đã được loại bỏ.

Không phải tất cả dữ liệu đều tích cực. Chỉ riêng ngày 6 tháng 10, khoảng 25.000 BTC đã được chuyển lên các sàn giao dịch, và thêm 5.300 BTC nữa được chuyển ròng trong khoảng thời gian từ ngày 8 đến ngày 11 tháng 10. Việc các đồng tiền này được chuyển lên sàn giao dịch có thể báo hiệu rằng người nắm giữ đang chuẩn bị bán.

Nhà phân tích đã tìm thấy hai yếu tố giữ cho Bitcoin ở mức giá cao. Đầu tiên là người mua giao ngay. Trên một CEX, tỷ lệ khối lượng giao dịch từ những người mua tích cực chỉ khoảng 49% vào ngày 7 và 8 tháng 10. Từ ngày 9 tháng 10, con số này đã đảo chiều lên 55,6%, sau đó là 52,7%, rồi 56,3%. Người mua đã tham gia ngay sau khi giá chạm đáy, trên thị trường giao ngay chứ không phải thị trường tương lai.

Thứ hai, và quan trọng nhất, là những người nắm giữ dài hạn. Khoảng 63% tổng số Bitcoin đã không được giao dịch trong hơn một năm. “Những đồng tiền đó không được bán ở mức giá 83.000, và chúng cũng không được bán ở mức giá 80.000,” ông nói. Khi các quỹ ETF bán 8.000 BTC vào một thị trường mà phần lớn nguồn cung đang đứng yên, tác động đến giá cả sẽ bị hạn chế.

Ông cũng chỉ ra mức giá trung bình thực sự của thị trường, chi phí trung bình của các nhà đầu tư năng động, vào khoảng 79.250 đô la. Mức thấp nhất của tuần trước đã dừng lại ngay trên mức này trước khi người mua tham gia.

Nhà phân tích nhìn thấy hai con đường và coi chúng có khả năng xảy ra như nhau.

Triển vọng tăng giá: Sự bật lên từ mức $80,944 bắt đầu một đợt tăng mạnh hơn, với mục tiêu ngắn hạn từ $84,177 đến $86,232. Sau đó, biểu đồ hàng ngày chỉ ra mức $88,597 đến $97,637. Quan điểm này sẽ không còn đúng nếu Bitcoin giảm xuống dưới $80,393. Lộ trình thận trọng: Đợt tăng giá hiện tại chỉ là sự bật lên tạm thời và sẽ dừng lại ở mức $84,956 đến $85,434, bên trong vùng kháng cự kéo dài đến $86,600. Nếu bị từ chối ở mức này, giá sẽ tiếp tục giảm. Việc giá vượt qua mốc 86.600 đô la một cách rõ rệt sẽ làm cho xu hướng tăng giá trở nên khả thi hơn.

Vùng hỗ trợ của nhà phân tích nằm trong khoảng từ 63.326 đô la đến 74.840 đô la. Ông nhấn mạnh đây không phải là mục tiêu, mà chỉ là vùng an toàn. Đỉnh của vùng này nằm gần hai mức giá quan trọng:

Chi phí trung bình của Strategy: 75.444 đô la Chi phí trung bình của người nắm giữ ngắn hạn: khoảng 74.400 đô la Ở mức giá đó, cả người nắm giữ lớn nhất trong doanh nghiệp và người mua mới trung bình đều sẽ hòa vốn. Việc họ giữ lại hay bắt đầu bán ra ở mức giá đó có thể quyết định bước đi lớn tiếp theo của Bitcoin. Nhà phân tích cho biết nếu có một đợt điều chỉnh sâu hơn, khu vực quanh mức 75.000 đô la là nơi ông có thể bắt đầu mua vào.
